Title: PCPJack Hijacks Cloud Servers for Covert SMTP Relay Network

Victim.Description: Compromised business servers across multiple regions.

diamond_model_summary: PCPJack is a sophisticated threat actor that hijacked cloud servers from major providers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure to create a covert SMTP relay network. The infrastructure includes a C2 server with open directories, Sliver and Chisel tools, and deployer scripts for Linux beacons. The operation's end goal remains unclear, but it supports large-scale email delivery.
doc_summary: The threat actor PCPJack has hijacked cloud servers from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure to create a covert SMTP email relay network. Compromised business servers across the United States, Europe, and Asia were converted into SMTP proxies. Hunt.io discovered source code, binaries, and a live Sliver configuration on an open C2 server. PCPJack was first identified by SentinelOne in April 2026, targeting cloud services with a credential theft framework. The infrastructure includes a Sliver-integrated SMTP proxy deployment toolkit, Chisel tunneling binaries, and deployer scripts for Linux beacons. The C2 server runs a Python script to verify Chisel tunnel ports for SMTP capability. Verified proxies are enriched with IP address data and synced to a downstream server. The operation's end goal remains unclear, but the infrastructure supports large-scale email delivery.
kill_chain_summary: PCPJack's attack involved reconnaissance to identify vulnerable cloud servers, weaponization through tool development, delivery of malicious binaries, exploitation of cloud server vulnerabilities, installation of persistence mechanisms, command and control via a C2 server, and actions on objectives by relaying SMTP traffic. The operation is sophisticated and opportunistic, leveraging compromised infrastructure for unknown purposes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: PCPJack's operation involves several indicators of compromise, including IP addresses of C2 servers, domain names used for SMTP relay, and tools like Sliver and Chisel. These indicators are critical for detection and remediation efforts. The operation's complexity and use of cloud infrastructure highlight the need for robust monitoring and defensive measures.

doc_summary: A Magecart campaign exploits Stripe's API and Google Tag Manager to steal credit card data from ecommerce checkout pages. The malware, discovered by Sansec, uses trusted domains googletagmanager.com and api.stripe.com to bypass security measures. The skimmer targets Magento/Adobe Commerce platforms, capturing sensitive payment information and storing it in Stripe customer records. A variant uses Google Firestore for data storage. The attack, active since at least December 24, 2025, highlights the need for enhanced security measures in ecommerce environments.
kill_chain_summary: The Magecart attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with the delivery of malicious code via Google Tag Manager containers. Detection and remediation require monitoring of GTM changes, API calls, and implementing strict security measures.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Magecart campaign presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. Domain names like googletagmanager.com and api.stripe.com are used for data exfiltration, making them difficult to block without affecting legitimate services. Title: Supply Chain Attack on Hola Browser Delivers Cryptocurrency Miner

Victim.Description: Users of the Windows version of Hola Browser.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a supply chain attack on Hola Browser, resulting in the delivery of a Monero cryptocurrency miner. The adversary's motivation appears to be financial gain through resource hijacking. The attack leveraged Hola's distribution infrastructure to deliver the miner to a small percentage of users. The victim is primarily Hola Browser users on Windows systems. The capability demonstrated includes persistence mechanisms and defensive evasion tactics.
doc_summary: The Windows version of Hola Browser, developed by the Israeli company Hola, was compromised in a supply chain attack. This attack delivered an undeclared executable identified as a Monero cryptocurrency miner. The compromise was discovered during AppEsteem certification checks. The miner, named 'me.exe', was found in the installation directory and was not certified, digitally signed, or timestamped. It added a Windows Defender exclusion rule, copied itself as 'HolaMonitorService.exe', and created an auto-starting Windows service. Hola confirmed the supply chain compromise, affecting about 0.1% of users, with no evidence of data theft. The company has since rebuilt its distribution pipeline and implemented advanced security measures. The incident was independently detected by cybersecurity firm Sygnia.
kill_chain_summary: The attack on Hola Browser follows a supply chain compromise model. The delivery stage involved the distribution of a malicious executable through Hola's update mechanism. Installation was achieved by creating an auto-starting Windows service. The final stage, actions on objectives, involved resource hijacking for cryptocurrency mining. Detection and remediation efforts focus on monitoring unauthorized services and unusual resource usage.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the identification of specific malware filenames such as 'me.exe' and 'HolaMonitorService.exe'. The adversary employed obfuscation techniques to evade detection. The primary tool used was a Monero cryptocurrency miner. Title: IronWorm Supply-Chain Attack on npm Packages

Victim.Description: Victims include developers and CI environments using infected npm packages.

diamond_model_summary: The IronWorm supply-chain attack on npm packages demonstrates a sophisticated adversary using Rust-based malware with eBPF rootkit capabilities. The attack targets developers and CI environments, leveraging stolen credentials to propagate trojanized packages. The infrastructure includes Tor for C2 communication, and the attack was initiated from a compromised npm account. The adversary's motivation appears to be financial, with a focus on credential theft and potential cryptocurrency access.
doc_summary: IronWorm is a Rust-based infostealer malware involved in a supply-chain attack on the Node Package Manager (npm) index, infecting 36 packages. It targets environment variables and credential files, including those for OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm. The malware uses an eBPF kernel rootkit for stealth and communicates over the Tor network. It self-propagates by exploiting stolen npm credentials, compromising developer and CI environments to publish trojanized packages. The attack was initiated from a compromised account named 'asteroiddao' and involved malicious commits with timestamps altered to evade detection. Although no direct link to Shai Hulud was found, similar commit names suggest a possible evolution of TeamPCP's payload. The attack was detected early and mitigated before spreading to more popular npm packages. Developers are advised to upgrade to fixed releases, rotate keys, and enable two-factor authentication. A similar attack involving JavaScript-based malware named binding.gyp was also observed.
kill_chain_summary: The IronWorm attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of Rust-based malware equipped with an eBPF rootkit. Delivery occurs through compromised npm packages, exploiting stolen credentials to execute and install trojanized packages in developer environments. Command and control is maintained via the Tor network, while actions on objectives focus on credential theft and malware propagation. The attack was detected early, preventing widespread impact.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The IronWorm attack presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain, with the use of unique malware hashes, Tor-based C2 infrastructure, and advanced rootkit techniques. Detection and response require identifying specific indicators such as compromised npm packages and altered commit timestamps. The attack's sophistication and use of stealth tactics highlight the need for robust monitoring and incident response capabilities.

Title: Cisco Unified Communications Manager Vulnerability CVE-2026-20230

Victim.Description: Organizations using Cisco Unified Communications Manager with WebDialer enabled

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, specifically a server-side request forgery that allows unauthenticated attackers to write files and escalate privileges to root. The adversary's capability is enhanced by the public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit. The infrastructure at risk includes systems running the WebDialer service, which is off by default but may be enabled in some deployments. Victims are organizations using Cisco Unified CM with WebDialer enabled, facing critical impact due to potential root access.
doc_summary: Cisco has patched a critical vulnerability in its Unified Communications Manager (CVE-2026-20230) that allows unauthenticated attackers to write files to the system and escalate privileges to root. The flaw is a server-side request forgery, and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. The vulnerability is only exploitable when the WebDialer service is running, which is off by default. Cisco has released a patch for version 14 (14SU6), but the fix for version 15 is not due until September 2026. The flaw is similar to previous vulnerabilities in Cisco's voice products, such as CVE-2025-20309 and CVE-2026-20045.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of a server-side request forgery vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, allowing attackers to gain initial access and escalate privileges to root. The exploitation stage is critical, with a CVSS score of 8.6, and the public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit increases the risk. Detection focuses on monitoring unusual HTTP requests and unauthorized file writes, while remediation involves applying patches and disabling the WebDialer service if not needed.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs, as the vulnerability CVE-2026-20230 represents a significant threat due to its potential for root access escalation. The public availability of a proof-of-concept exploit increases the difficulty of defense, as adversaries can easily replicate the attack. Detection and remediation efforts should focus on monitoring HTTP requests and applying patches to mitigate the risk.

Title: Anthropic's Claude Code GitHub Action Vulnerability Exploitation

Victim.Description: Public repositories using Anthropic's Claude Code GitHub Action were vulnerable to exploitation.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to broad permissions and insufficient trigger checks.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved an adversary exploiting a vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Code GitHub Action. The adversary, identified as RyotaK, used prompt injection techniques to gain unauthorized access to public repositories. The capability involved exploiting GitHub App registration and prompt injection vulnerabilities. The infrastructure targeted was GitHub's platform, specifically public repositories using the vulnerable action. The victims were repositories in the technology sector, with a high impact severity due to potential unauthorized code execution and data exfiltration.
doc_summary: A security researcher identified a vulnerability in Anthropic's Claude Code GitHub Action, allowing attackers to exploit public repositories by opening a GitHub issue. The flaw, reported by RyotaK of GMO Flatt Security, involved bypassing trigger checks for GitHub Apps, enabling prompt injection attacks. The vulnerability was fixed in claude-code-action v1.0.94. The attack could lead to unauthorized code execution and data exfiltration, posing a supply chain risk. Anthropic rated the issue with a CVSS score of 7.8 and issued a bug bounty. The incident highlights the risks of broad permissions and prompt injection in AI-driven CI/CD workflows.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable repositories. Weaponization involved crafting a GitHub issue with embedded prompt injection commands. Delivery was achieved by submitting the issue to the target repository. Exploitation occurred when the adversary executed unauthorized commands through the vulnerability. Command and control were established by gaining control over the repository's workflow execution. Actions on objectives included accessing sensitive data and potentially modifying code. The incident highlights the risks of broad permissions and prompt injection in AI-driven CI/CD workflows.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools such as GitHub App and prompt injection techniques. The TTPs employed involved exploiting GitHub App registration and prompt injection vulnerabilities. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified. The incident underscores the challenges of detecting and mitigating prompt injection attacks in AI-driven environments. The scoring reflects the presence of tools and TTPs, emphasizing the need for robust detection and remediation strategies to address such vulnerabilities.

Title: Dismantling of Online Marketplace for Fake Identity Documents in the EU

Victim.Description: European Union member states affected by document fraud.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary operating an online marketplace for counterfeit identity documents, targeting the European Union. The capability includes document-production equipment, and the infrastructure is an online platform. The victim is the EU, with government sectors affected by document fraud.
doc_summary: French and Spanish authorities dismantled an online marketplace selling fake identity documents to migrant smuggling rings within the European Union. On May 27, law enforcement arrested a suspect in Alicante, Spain, seizing document-production equipment and approximately 800 counterfeit European identity documents. The investigation began after French authorities identified a website advertising counterfeit identity documents, tracing the suspect to Alicante. The suspect allegedly administered a marketplace offering forged identity and administrative documents to customers across Europe, facilitating migrant smuggling operations by supplying criminal networks with fraudulent documents to evade border controls and obtain residence rights. Europol expanded its capacity to combat migrant smuggling in March 2026, following a 2025 EU Serious and Organised Crime Threat Assessment that flagged document fraud as a main enabler of fraudulent legalization of residency and migrant smuggling within the EU.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves reconnaissance to identify demand for counterfeit documents, weaponization through document creation, delivery via an online marketplace, and exploitation by using these documents to bypass security controls. Actions on objectives include facilitating migrant smuggling operations.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools such as document-production equipment and TTPs related to document fraud. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The focus is on the infrastructure and capabilities used to produce and distribute counterfeit documents.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager

Victim.Description: Organizations using Cisco Unified Communications Manager with WebDialer service enabled

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager, allowing remote attackers to gain root privileges through SSRF attacks. The adversary can exploit this vulnerability by sending crafted HTTP requests to affected devices. The infrastructure at risk includes systems with the WebDialer service enabled, which is disabled by default. Victims are organizations using Cisco Unified CM with this service enabled. The capability involves exploiting CVE-2026-20230, with no specific adversary identified.
doc_summary: Cisco has released a critical security update for a vulnerability in the Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM), previously known as Cisco CallManager. This flaw allows attackers to gain root privileges through a low-complexity server-side request forgery (SSRF) attack. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-20230, can be exploited remotely without privileges. Cisco's Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is aware of publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code but has not found evidence of active exploitation. The vulnerability affects systems with the WebDialer service enabled, which is disabled by default. Administrators are advised to install Cisco Unified CM versions 14SU6 or 15SU5 and can disable the WebDialer service as a temporary measure. The vulnerability has been assigned a Security Impact Rating (SIR) of Critical.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation stage, where attackers leverage a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Cisco Unified Communications Manager to gain root privileges. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-20230, can be exploited remotely without prior access. Detection involves monitoring HTTP requests and unauthorized file writes, while remediation includes applying security patches and disabling the WebDialer service. No significant activity was detected in other stages of the kill chain.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs, as the exploitation of CVE-2026-20230 is the key indicator. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified, making detection reliant on monitoring HTTP requests and unauthorized file writes. The lack of specific indicators like hashes or IPs means the Pyramid of Pain score is low, emphasizing the need for behavioral detection and timely patching.

Title: Espionage Campaign Targeting Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox

Victim.Description: The victim was a senior executive at a major global stock exchange.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an unknown adversary conducting a sophisticated espionage campaign against a senior executive at a global stock exchange. The adversary used advanced capabilities to exfiltrate data stealthily over several months, leveraging legitimate cloud services like Dropbox and OneDrive to blend in with normal traffic. The victim's Outlook mailbox was targeted, containing sensitive market-moving information. The infrastructure used included cloud services and hard-coded IP addresses to avoid detection. The attack's motivation was espionage, aiming to gather intelligence on the executive's dealings and the organization's strategic direction.
doc_summary: Unknown attackers infiltrated the Outlook mailbox of a senior executive at a major global stock exchange, maintaining access for five months. The attackers used Dropbox and OneDrive for data exfiltration, blending traffic with normal cloud activity. Symantec and Carbon Black identified the campaign as espionage, not financially motivated. The attackers employed tools like Aspose for mailbox stealing, FRPC for tunneling, and Secretsdump for credential theft. The operation began with lateral movement from a compromised device, using binaries disguised as Adobe and OneDrive updaters. The attackers avoided detection by mimicking legitimate services and using hard-coded Microsoft IP addresses. The campaign ended with a staged but unused backdoor, suggesting lost access. Attribution remains unresolved due to the use of public tools and consumer cloud services.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify the executive's mailbox as a valuable target. Weaponization involved preparing tools for data exfiltration and credential theft. Delivery was achieved through lateral movement from a compromised device. Exploitation involved running binaries as SYSTEM to gain full control. Installation included deploying a mailbox stealer and other tools. Command and control were maintained using Dropbox and OneDrive, avoiding detection by blending with normal traffic. Actions on objectives involved exfiltrating mailbox data over several months, gathering intelligence on market-moving information.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators. Hash values of the tools used, such as Aspose and FRPC, are at the bottom of the pyramid. IP addresses used for command and control, particularly hard-coded Microsoft IPs, are more challenging to change. Domain names were not explicitly mentioned, but the use of Dropbox and OneDrive is significant. Network host artifacts include scheduled tasks mimicking legitimate services. Tools like Aspose, FRPC, and Secretsdump are critical components of the attack. TTPs include data exfiltration via cloud services and credential theft, representing the highest level of pain for the adversary.

Title: Large-Scale Operation Impersonating Open-Source Projects for Malware Distribution

Victim.Description: Users searching for open-source tools like Ghidra, dnSpy, and SpiderFoot.
Victim.Geography: Turkey, Poland, Brazil, Germany, France, Russia, United Kingdom
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to impersonation and redirection attacks.

diamond_model_summary: The adversary in this incident is conducting a sophisticated operation impersonating open-source projects to distribute malware. The capability involves using fake sites and a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) to redirect users and deliver malware. The infrastructure includes CloudFront-hosted scripts and fake domains mimicking popular tools. Victims are primarily users searching for open-source tools, with a high impact severity due to the impersonation and redirection tactics employed.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a large-scale operation impersonating open-source and freeware projects to distribute malware via a Traffic Distribution System (TDS). The operation involves well-designed fake sites mimicking trusted tools like Ghidra, dnSpy, and SpiderFoot. These sites use CloudFront-hosted JavaScript to redirect users to a TDS, which enforces strict gating mechanisms. The campaign targets users searching for these tools on search engines, leading to high search rankings for the fake sites. The TDS infrastructure was repurposed for malware distribution starting January 2026, delivering malware families such as Remus Stealer, AnimateClipper, and SessionGate. The operation primarily affects users in Turkey, Poland, Brazil, Germany, France, Russia, and the United Kingdom. The final payload communicates with external servers to download and execute additional malware.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves reconnaissance to identify popular open-source projects, weaponization through the creation of fake sites, delivery via redirection to a TDS, and installation of malware on victim systems. Command and control is established through communication with external servers, and actions on objectives involve gathering system information. The operation is sophisticated, leveraging search engine manipulation and advanced TDS mechanisms to achieve its goals.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names of fake sites, tools like CloudFront-hosted JavaScript and TDS, and TTPs such as impersonation and redirection. The operation's sophistication is evident in its use of advanced techniques to evade detection and deliver malware. The infrastructure's complexity and the adversary's ability to manipulate search engine rankings make this a challenging threat to mitigate.

Title: Large-Scale Operation Impersonating Open-Source Projects for Malware Distribution

Victim.Description: Users searching for open-source tools like Ghidra, dnSpy, and SpiderFoot.
Victim.Geography: Turkey, Poland, Brazil, Germany, France, Russia, United Kingdom
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to impersonation and redirection attacks.

diamond_model_summary: The adversary in this incident is conducting a sophisticated operation impersonating open-source projects to distribute malware. The capability involves using fake sites and a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) to redirect users and deliver malware. The infrastructure includes CloudFront-hosted scripts and fake domains mimicking popular tools. Victims are primarily users searching for open-source tools, with a high impact severity due to the impersonation and redirection tactics employed.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a large-scale operation impersonating open-source and freeware projects to distribute malware via a Traffic Distribution System (TDS). The operation involves well-designed fake sites mimicking trusted tools like Ghidra, dnSpy, and SpiderFoot. These sites use CloudFront-hosted JavaScript to redirect users to a TDS, which enforces strict gating mechanisms. The campaign targets users searching for these tools on search engines, leading to high search rankings for the fake sites. The TDS infrastructure was repurposed for malware distribution starting January 2026, delivering malware families such as Remus Stealer, AnimateClipper, and SessionGate. The operation primarily affects users in Turkey, Poland, Brazil, Germany, France, Russia, and the United Kingdom. The final payload communicates with external servers to download and execute additional malware.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves reconnaissance to identify popular open-source projects, weaponization through the creation of fake sites, delivery via redirection to a TDS, and installation of malware on victim systems. Command and control is established through communication with external servers, and actions on objectives involve gathering system information. The operation is sophisticated, leveraging search engine manipulation and advanced TDS mechanisms to achieve its goals.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names of fake sites, tools like CloudFront-hosted JavaScript and TDS, and TTPs such as impersonation and redirection. The operation's sophistication is evident in its use of advanced techniques to evade detection and deliver malware. The infrastructure's complexity and the adversary's ability to manipulate search engine rankings make this a challenging threat to mitigate.

Title: Operation FlutterBridge: macOS Malvertising Campaign

Victim.Description: macOS users targeted through malvertising campaigns.
Victim.Geography: United States, Canada, Australia, France, Germany
Victim.Security_Posture: Compromised due to valid Apple Developer IDs and notarization

diamond_model_summary: Operation FlutterBridge is a sophisticated macOS malvertising campaign by the cybercrime group CL-CRI-1089. The campaign uses the FlutterShell backdoor, built with the Flutter framework, to infect targets with adware and execute shell commands. The infrastructure involves a network of Google-verified shell companies distributing malicious ads. Victims are macOS users in the United States, Canada, Australia, France, and Germany. The campaign highlights the persistent danger of malvertising and the sophistication of CL-CRI-1089's tactics.
doc_summary: Operation FlutterBridge is a macOS malvertising campaign spreading the FlutterShell backdoor. The campaign is linked to the cybercrime group CL-CRI-1089, active since 2023. FlutterShell, built using the Flutter framework, infects targets with adware and possesses backdoor capabilities, including shell command execution and file system manipulation. The campaign uses trojanized productivity software and malicious Google and YouTube ads distributed by shell companies like AdsParkPro LTD and Advantage Web Marketing LLC. Targeting macOS users in the United States, Canada, Australia, France, and Germany, the campaign's latest iteration was detected in March 2026. FlutterShell's WebView-based architecture allows dynamic behavior changes without recompilation. The campaign highlights the persistent danger of malvertising and the sophistication of CL-CRI-1089's tactics.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for Operation FlutterBridge involves reconnaissance to identify target demographics, weaponization through the development of the FlutterShell backdoor, delivery via malicious ads and trojanized software, exploitation of user trust, installation of the backdoor, command and control using WebView-based architecture, and actions on objectives including shell command execution and data exfiltration. The campaign demonstrates a high level of sophistication and persistence.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: Operation FlutterBridge presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. The use of valid Apple Developer IDs and notarization complicates detection at the hash level. The WebView-based architecture allows dynamic behavior changes, making domain and IP-based detection difficult. The campaign's reliance on malvertising and trojanized software highlights the need for robust detection and remediation strategies. The persistent and sophisticated nature of the campaign underscores the importance of continuous monitoring and threat intelligence.

doc_summary: The U.S. Department of Justice announced a major operation called Disruption Week, targeting cyber-enabled and cryptocurrency fraud. The operation, which began on May 18, 2026, involved the takedown of millions of accounts used by transnational cybercrime groups in Southeast Asia. Private sector companies froze over $3.8 million in cryptocurrency linked to these scams. The Scam Center Strike Force aims to dismantle criminal organizations running fraud and pig butchering scams, often involving human trafficking. The operation included participation from major tech companies and international law enforcement agencies. Cryptocurrency investment scams have caused significant financial losses, with reported losses rising from $3.96 billion in 2023 to over $7.2 billion in 2025. The operation highlights the need for international collaboration to combat transnational online fraud.
kill_chain_summary: The operation against cyber-enabled fraud involved several stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Reconnaissance was conducted to identify potential victims, followed by the delivery of fraudulent investment platforms through social engineering. Victims were exploited by depositing funds into these platforms, and the adversaries laundered the stolen funds through cryptocurrency. The operation highlights the need for international collaboration to combat such sophisticated fraud schemes.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes various indicators such as fraudulent domains and accounts used for scams. Title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-45247 in Mirasvit Cache Warmer

Victim.Description: Magento stores using Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension.
Victim.Geography: United States, United Kingdom, France, Australia

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves unknown adversaries exploiting a critical deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-45247) in the Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension for Magento. The adversaries use serialized PHP object payloads to achieve remote code execution on targeted servers. The infrastructure involves HTTP requests carrying malicious payloads, primarily targeting e-commerce sites in the United States, United Kingdom, France, and Australia. Victims are Magento stores using the vulnerable extension, with a critical impact severity due to potential server compromise.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added a critical flaw impacting Mirasvit Cache Warmer, a popular Magento full-page cache extension, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-45247, is a deserialization of untrusted data that could be exploited to execute arbitrary PHP code on an affected server. The flaw impacts all versions of the extension prior to version 1.11.12, with patches released on May 25, 2026. Sansec reported that the vulnerability could be exploited by any storefront request carrying a crafted CacheWarmer cookie, leading to remote code execution. Imperva observed active attack activity exploiting this vulnerability through serialized PHP object payloads. The attacks primarily targeted gaming and business sites in the United States, United Kingdom, France, and Australia. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies were ordered to apply the fixes by June 6, 2026.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable Magento stores using the Mirasvit Cache Warmer extension. Adversaries then weaponize serialized PHP object payloads to exploit the deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-45247). The payloads are delivered via HTTP requests, leading to exploitation and remote code execution. The attack primarily targets e-commerce sites, with the objective of executing arbitrary commands on compromised servers. Detection involves monitoring for CacheWarmer cookies with Base64-encoded serialized objects, while remediation includes applying patches and deploying web application firewalls.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes serialized PHP object payloads as tools, HTTP requests as network host artifacts, and the exploitation of CVE-2026-45247 as a TTP. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified. The scoring reflects the presence of tools and TTPs, indicating a moderate level of difficulty for adversaries to change their tactics. Detection and remediation efforts should focus on identifying and blocking malicious payloads and applying patches to vulnerable software.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, facilitating transactions linked to the IRGC and ransomware actors. The U.S. Treasury's OFAC imposed sanctions as part of the 'Economic Fury' campaign. doc_summary: The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has imposed sanctions on Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, for facilitating payments related to terrorist activities. Nobitex is accused of helping evade economic sanctions and facilitating transactions linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The sanctions are part of the U.S. government's 'Economic Fury' campaign and also target three other Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges: Wallex, Bitpin, and Ramzinex. Nobitex processed over 50% of Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025, with significant transactions tied to the IRGC and ransomware actors. The sanctions freeze any assets under U.S. jurisdiction and prohibit U.S. persons from doing business with the designated entities. The Iranian cryptocurrency ecosystem received nearly $7.8 billion in 2025, with IRGC-associated addresses accounting for over 50% of the value in Q4 2025. In June 2025, the pro-Israel hacking group 'Predatory Sparrow' claimed to have breached Nobitex, stealing digital assets and leaving politically-tinted messages.
kill_chain_summary: The incident involves Nobitex facilitating transactions for the IRGC and ransomware actors. The reconnaissance stage involved identifying Nobitex as a key player in facilitating IRGC transactions. The actions on objectives stage involved Nobitex facilitating transactions for IRGC and ransomware actors. The sanctions imposed by OFAC aim to disrupt these activities and prevent further financial support for terrorist activities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The incident lacks specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains. diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors targeting internet-exposed Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) systems in critical infrastructure sectors. The adversary, potentially linked to Iranian hackers, exploits vulnerabilities such as authentication bypass and SQL injection to gain access and modify system settings. The infrastructure includes ATG systems used in sectors like Energy, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Transportation Systems. Victims are organizations in these sectors, primarily in the United States, facing high exposure potential due to weak authentication and internet-exposed systems.
doc_summary: CISA, FBI, NSA, and the Department of Energy warn of cyber attacks targeting internet-exposed Automatic Tank Gauge (ATG) systems used in critical infrastructure sectors like Energy, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Transportation Systems. Hackers exploit authentication bypass vulnerabilities, hardcoded credentials, OS command-execution flaws, SQL injection vulnerabilities, and privilege-escalation weaknesses to gain access. Attackers modify system settings, alter network configurations, and disable alerts, risking leaks or equipment failures. The advisory does not attribute the activity to a specific threat actor, but CNN reports suggest Iranian hackers may be involved. Organizations are urged to block ATG systems from the internet, restrict remote access, replace default passwords, use strong credentials and multifactor authentication, apply security updates, and monitor systems for unauthorized changes.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with reconnaissance to identify internet-exposed ATG systems. Exploitation occurs through vulnerabilities like authentication bypass and SQL injection, allowing attackers to gain initial access. Actions on objectives involve modifying system settings and disabling alerts, potentially causing operational disruptions. The attack highlights the need for improved security measures, including network segmentation, strong authentication, and regular system audits.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as authentication bypass, SQL injection, and command execution, which are challenging for defenders to address. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names were identified, limiting the ability to block or detect the attack using traditional indicators. The focus should be on addressing the underlying vulnerabilities and improving security posture to prevent similar attacks.

Title: HTTP/2 Bomb DoS Attack on Major Web Servers

Victim.Description: Web servers running HTTP/2 protocol configurations are vulnerable to the attack.

diamond_model_summary: The HTTP/2 Bomb DoS attack represents a significant threat to web servers using default HTTP/2 configurations. The adversary, identified as Calif, employs a combination of HPACK compression amplification and Slowloris-style resource retention to exhaust server resources. The attack targets major web servers like NGINX, Apache, Microsoft IIS, Envoy, and Cloudflare Pingora, exploiting vulnerabilities in the HTTP/2 protocol. The impact is high, with the potential to render servers inaccessible within seconds. Mitigation involves disabling HTTP/2, applying patches, and using proxies/firewalls.
doc_summary: A new denial-of-service (DoS) attack named HTTP/2 Bomb can be executed from a single machine to incapacitate web servers within seconds. This attack affects default HTTP/2 configurations of major web servers like NGINX, Apache HTTP Server, Microsoft IIS, Envoy, and Cloudflare Pingora. Discovered by OpenAI's Codex software agent with Calif researchers, the attack combines HPACK compression amplification and Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling. A single client on a 100 Mbps connection can exhaust tens of gigabytes of RAM in seconds, forcing the server to allocate it and preventing its release. The attack abuses the HPACK mechanism for header compression, resulting in significant server-side memory allocation. The attack also prevents memory from being freed by advertising a zero-byte flow-control window. Patches have been released for some platforms, such as nginx version 1.29.8 and Apache httpd mod_http2 2.0.41, but not for IIS, Envoy, or Pingora. Disabling HTTP/2 and using proxies/firewalls are recommended mitigations.
kill_chain_summary: The HTTP/2 Bomb DoS attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of HPACK compression amplification and Slowloris-style resource retention. The attack is delivered via HTTP/2 requests, exploiting protocol vulnerabilities to exhaust server resources. The adversary achieves denial of service by preventing memory from being freed, causing server resource exhaustion. The attack impacts major web servers, with high severity due to the potential for rapid service disruption. Mitigation strategies include disabling HTTP/2, applying patches, and using proxies/firewalls.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The HTTP/2 Bomb DoS attack presents challenges in detection and mitigation due to its exploitation of protocol vulnerabilities. The attack does not rely on specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names, making traditional detection methods less effective. Instead, it leverages HTTP/2 protocol features, such as HPACK compression and flow-control stalling, to achieve its objectives. Mitigation requires a focus on protocol-level defenses, such as disabling HTTP/2, applying patches, and using proxies/firewalls with header-count limits. The attack's reliance on protocol features highlights the need for advanced detection and mitigation strategies.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a spear-phishing campaign by the Pakistan-aligned SideCopy group targeting Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance using Xeno RAT. doc_summary: Hackers are exploiting an authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-35616 in FortiClient Enterprise Management Server EMS to deliver an undocumented credential stealer called EKZ. The attacker disguised the malware as an update for Fortinet endpoints and executed it through VPN scripting workflows managed by FortiClient. The exploited critical vulnerability is an improper access control flaw that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or commands via specially crafted requests. Fortinet released emergency hotfixes for versions 7.4.5 and 7.4.6 of the product. CISA reacted quickly to the malicious activity. The Shadowserver Foundation reported 2,000 internet-exposed EMS instances. Arctic Wolf observed attacks leveraging the vulnerability to deliver the EKZ infostealer. The intrusion begins with abusing endpoint APIs to perform administrative actions without authentication. The attacker modifies the EMS configuration and VPN policies to introduce the execution of malicious scripts. The legitimate fortitray.exe launched malicious batch scripts through Command Prompt. Those scripts executed a base64-encoded PowerShell payload that downloaded and ran malware disguised as a Fortinet patch, then exfiltrated data to an attacker-controlled VPS over HTTP. The downloaded payload, tracked as EKZ Infostealer, targets both Chromium-based and Firefox web browsers and extracts stored data to text files while bypassing encrypted password protections. The malware targets credentials, credit card details, addresses, phone numbers, and cookies, which provide access to accounts protected by multi-factor authentication.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-35616, allowing the adversary to execute arbitrary code. The malware is delivered disguised as a Fortinet update, leading to the installation of EKZ Infostealer via PowerShell scripts. Title: Unpatched Zero-Day Vulnerability in Gogs Allows Remote Code Execution

Victim.Description: Gogs servers with default configurations

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a zero-day vulnerability in Gogs, allowing remote code execution by exploiting default configurations. The adversary can create accounts and repositories due to open registration, leading to potential server compromise. doc_summary: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability in the Gogs self-hosted Git service allows attackers to gain remote code execution on Internet-facing instances. This critical security flaw affects the latest release versions (Gogs 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev) and can be exploited by authenticated attackers without admin privileges. The vulnerability was discovered by Rapid7 senior security researcher Jonah Burgess and affects all Gogs servers with default configurations. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely via pull requests that use a malicious branch name during the 'Rebase before merging' operation. The vulnerability was reported to Gogs maintainers on March 17, but no patch has been provided. Shadowserver tracks exposed instances, most of them in Asia and Europe. The vulnerability poses significant risks, allowing attackers to compromise servers, read repositories, dump credentials, and pivot to other systems.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in Gogs, allowing remote code execution. diamond_model_summary: The incident involves adversaries leveraging a significant C2 infrastructure in the Middle East, particularly in Saudi Arabia, to conduct malicious activities. The adversaries' strategic objective is to maintain control over compromised systems, with a high level of sophistication evident in their use of advanced tools and malware.
doc_summary: Hunt.io identified over 1,350 command-and-control (C2) servers across 98 Middle East infrastructure providers from February 1 to May 1, 2026. Saudi Arabia's STC hosts 981 C2 servers, representing 72.4% of the region's C2 infrastructure. IoT-focused botnets like Hajime, Mozi, and Mirai, along with offensive frameworks such as Tactical RMM, Cobalt Strike, and Sliver, dominate the malware landscape in the Middle East. The report highlights the overwhelming presence of C2 infrastructure, accounting for 96.8% of malicious activity, far surpassing phishing and publicly reported IOCs. This indicates a significant threat landscape in the region, with Saudi Arabia being a major hub for C2 operations.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves reconnaissance to identify vulnerable infrastructure, weaponization of IoT botnets and offensive frameworks, delivery of malware via compromised devices, exploitation of vulnerabilities, installation of malware, establishment of C2 channels, and actions on objectives such as data exfiltration. pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of specific tools like Tactical RMM, Cobalt Strike, and Sliver, as well as malware families such as Hajime, Mozi, and Mirai. The high level of sophistication and extensive infrastructure presence indicate a formidable threat landscape in the Middle East.

Title: Kimsuky Cyber Attacks on South Korean Military and Corporate Entities

Victim.Description: South Korean military and corporate entities targeted by Kimsuky.

diamond_model_summary: The Kimsuky threat actor, also known as Velvet Chollima, targeted South Korean military and corporate entities using advanced social engineering tactics and malware delivery techniques. The campaign involved fake web pages and malware such as HTTPSpy, PebbleDash, and AppleSeed. Kimsuky leveraged tools like PowerShell and VS Code tunneling to establish persistence and control over compromised systems. The attacks were sophisticated, indicating a high level of capability and motivation for espionage and data exfiltration.
doc_summary: The North Korean state-sponsored threat actor Kimsuky, also known as Velvet Chollima, has been linked to cyber attacks targeting South Korean military and corporate entities in March and April 2026. Kimsuky employed social engineering tactics, including spoofing security software installation pages and crafting fake Webex meeting pages. The attacks delivered a variant of the HTTPSpy malware disguised as installers from South Korean security software. The campaign involved malicious payloads propagated through bogus web pages impersonating security software installation pages. The malware used included nos-setup.exe and astx-setup.exe, which launched a second-stage DLL payload via regsvr32.exe. The DLL established persistence and contacted a command-and-control server. Another campaign involved a counterfeit Webex page urging victims to download a script, resulting in the deployment of an intermediate downloader using PowerShell. The malware families PebbleDash and AppleSeed were also delivered. Kimsuky leveraged VS Code tunneling and DWAgent for post-exploitation activities, affecting various sectors in South Korea.
kill_chain_summary: Kimsuky's attack on South Korean entities followed a structured kill chain. The reconnaissance phase involved gathering information on potential targets. Weaponization included crafting fake web pages and malware payloads. Delivery was executed through social engineering tactics, leading to exploitation via user trust. Installation involved deploying malware disguised as legitimate software. Command and control were maintained through C2 servers, enabling actions on objectives such as data exfiltration and remote access. The campaign demonstrated Kimsuky's advanced capabilities and strategic objectives.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Kimsuky incident includes various indicators. Hash values of malware files like nos-setup.exe and astx-setup.exe are at the base. Domain names and IP addresses used for C2 communication are critical for detection. Network host artifacts, such as regsvr32.exe and fix-camera.jse, provide insight into the attack's execution. Tools like PowerShell and VS Code tunneling are significant for understanding the adversary's capabilities. TTPs, including social engineering and malware delivery, highlight the sophistication of Kimsuky's operations.

Title: Critical RCE Vulnerability in Gogs Git Service

Victim.Description: Victims are users of Gogs Git service across various platforms.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Gogs, allowing remote code execution by authenticated users. The adversary can exploit this flaw without admin privileges, using a crafted branch name to inject malicious code during a git rebase operation. The infrastructure affected includes all Gogs instances, with potential victims being any users of the service. The capability to exploit this vulnerability is facilitated by a Metasploit module developed by Rapid7.
doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability in Gogs, an open-source self-hosted Git service, allows authenticated users to execute arbitrary code. Rated 9.4 on the CVSS scale, the flaw enables remote code execution via a malicious branch name in a pull request, exploiting the --exec flag in git rebase. The vulnerability, disclosed by Rapid7 and researcher Jonah Burgess, does not require admin privileges and affects all platforms, including Windows, Linux, and macOS. Despite being reported on March 17, 2026, it remains unpatched, posing risks of server breaches, credential dumping, and cross-tenant data breaches. Rapid7 has developed a Metasploit module to automate the exploit.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the adversary gaining initial access by creating an account on a Gogs instance. Weaponization occurs through crafting a malicious branch name to exploit the vulnerability. Exploitation is achieved by executing arbitrary code via the --exec flag in git rebase. The attacker can then perform actions on objectives, such as accessing repositories, dumping credentials, and causing cross-tenant data breaches. The vulnerability remains unpatched, increasing the risk of widespread exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of a specific command line (--exec) as a TTP, which is challenging to change and thus impactful for detection and response. The Metasploit tool is also a significant indicator, as it automates the exploit process. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains are identified, limiting the scope of easily actionable indicators. The focus should be on detecting the use of the --exec flag in git rebase operations.

doc_summary: Dutch authorities, in collaboration with the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), have dismantled a massive botnet operation involving 17 million compromised devices. The botnet was linked to a service called Asocks, advertising itself as a universal proxy service with millions of IP addresses. The investigation revealed that the devices were unknowingly part of the botnet, used for illegal activities such as DDoS attacks and cryptocurrency mining. The authorities have not received a response from Asocks regarding the allegations. To prevent such infections, it is recommended to change default credentials, apply firmware updates, and disable unnecessary remote administration.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting a critical vulnerability in FortiClient EMS to deliver EKZ Infostealer malware. The adversary used sophisticated techniques, including API access bypass and PowerShell-based malware delivery, to target managed endpoints. The infrastructure included a C2 server at IP 83.138.53.110, and the victim assets were primarily managed endpoints. The attack aimed to steal credentials and sensitive data from browsers, highlighting the adversary's strategic objective of accessing sensitive information.
doc_summary: Threat actors exploited a critical vulnerability CVE-2026-35616 in FortiClient Endpoint Management Server (EMS) to deliver EKZ Infostealer malware. The attack involved bypassing API authentication, using FortiClient's management pathway to push malicious PowerShell commands, and disguising the payload as a Fortinet update. The malware targeted managed endpoints, stealing credentials and sensitive data from browsers. The attack leveraged fortitray.exe to execute a Base64-encoded PowerShell script, exfiltrating data to 83.138.53[.]110. The vulnerability was patched in FortiClient EMS 7.4.7. Arctic Wolf observed the campaign in May 2026, highlighting the threat actors' ability to modify EMS-managed configurations and execute scripts on endpoints.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, starting with the exploitation of CVE-2026-35616 to gain initial access and escalate privileges. The delivery stage involved using FortiClient EMS to push a disguised malware update, executed via PowerShell. Installation of EKZ Infostealer on endpoints allowed for persistence, while command and control were maintained through HTTP POST requests to a C2 server. The final stage involved actions on objectives, specifically credential theft and data exfiltration from browsers. Detection and remediation efforts focused on monitoring PowerShell activity, applying patches, and restricting network access.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators: a specific IP address (83.138.53.110) used for C2 communication, the use of PowerShell scripts for execution, and the EKZ Infostealer malware. These indicators provide varying levels of difficulty for adversaries to change, with IP addresses and tools being more challenging to alter than hash values. The incident highlights the importance of monitoring network traffic and script execution to detect and respond to such threats effectively.

doc_summary: A new campaign by the threat actor JINX-0164 targets cryptocurrency organizations using recruitment-themed social engineering and bespoke macOS malware. The campaign involves sophisticated techniques to move laterally from compromised employee laptops to code distribution systems and development infrastructure. The threat actor uses LinkedIn profiles to lure victims into downloading a Python-based macOS infostealer and remote access trojan named AUDIOFIX. The malware steals sensitive data, including credentials from password managers, web browsers, and iCloud Keychain files. The campaign also involves a Go-based backdoor called MiniRAT, distributed via a compromised npm package. The attack is reminiscent of North Korean threat clusters but lacks direct infrastructure overlaps.

Weaponization involves the development of custom macOS malware. Delivery is achieved via fake teleconference domains, leading to exploitation through social engineering. Title: Notepad++ Version 8.9.6.1 Security Vulnerabilities

Victim.Description: Users of Notepad++ versions up to 8.9.6

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves vulnerabilities in Notepad++ that allow arbitrary code execution through configuration file manipulation. The primary vulnerability, CVE-2026-48778, is an OS Command Injection flaw. Attackers can exploit this by modifying the config.xml file or using social engineering to trick users into executing malicious code. The vulnerabilities highlight the risks of improper input validation and configuration handling in software applications.
doc_summary: Notepad++ has released version 8.9.6.1 to address multiple security vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow arbitrary code execution. The update, published on May 26, 2026, patches three vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-48770, CVE-2026-48778, and CVE-2026-48800. These issues affect versions up to 8.9.6 and highlight risks tied to improper handling of configuration files. The most severe issue, CVE-2026-48778, stems from how Notepad++ processes the config.xml file, specifically the <GUIConfig name="commandLineInterpreter"> parameter. This behavior allows an attacker to control what executable is launched through the application. Attackers can modify the %APPDATA%\Notepad++\config.xml file or distribute malicious shortcut files leveraging the -settingsDir parameter. Additional scenarios include poisoning cloud-synced configuration paths or using social engineering techniques. CVE-2026-48770 is a crash vulnerability causing denial-of-service conditions, while CVE-2026-48800 is related to improper handling of shortcuts.xml. Users are advised to upgrade to Notepad++ version 8.9.6.1 immediately.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in Notepad++ configuration files, specifically targeting the config.xml file. doc_summary: Microsoft has identified an active cryptojacking campaign leveraging AI chatbot interactions to direct users to malicious download sites. The campaign impersonates legitimate system utilities like CrystalDiskInfo and HWMonitor, targeting users with high-performance GPUs. The threat actors establish persistent remote access using ScreenConnect, enabling data theft and lateral movement. The attack chain involves SEO poisoning and AI search result poisoning, with over 150 malicious domains identified. The downloaded ZIP file contains a legitimate executable and a rogue DLL, which installs ScreenConnect. The campaign uses PowerShell scripts for binary delivery and employs process hollowing for mining code execution. The attack highlights the adaptation of social engineering and monetization strategies to modern user behavior.

The attack leveraged shared machine keys for ViewState deserialization attacks, indicating a high level of sophistication and potential state-sponsored involvement.
doc_summary: Hackers exploited a zero-day vulnerability in the KnowledgeDeliver LMS, deploying the Godzilla web shell. The flaw, a deserialization issue, was exploited without authentication due to a shared hardcoded machine key in the web portal configuration. Mandiant responded to an attack in late 2025, noting the vulnerability was initially exploited as a zero-day to inject a malicious script. The use of identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys across deployments facilitated the attack. The malicious code convinced users to download a fake installer, leading to Cobalt Strike beacon infections. The threat actor deployed the .NET-based Godzilla web shell, also used in 2024. Researchers noted ViewState deserialization attacks targeting financial sector companies. The attackers modified JavaScript files to prompt users to install a fake security plugin, loading malicious scripts from attacker-controlled domains. Over the past year, similar attacks targeted various web platforms.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with the exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in the KnowledgeDeliver LMS. The adversary weaponized the attack by crafting malicious ViewState payloads, delivered via compromised web servers. Exploitation allowed remote code execution, leading to the installation of the Godzilla web shell and Cobalt Strike beacon. Command and control were established using web protocols, and actions on objectives included modifying files and escalating control over the server.

doc_summary: The Iranian hacking group MuddyWater has launched a new campaign affecting nine organizations across nine countries in early 2026. The campaign targeted sectors such as industrial manufacturing, electronics, education, public sector, financial services, and professional services. Notable victims include a South Korean electronics manufacturer and a Middle Eastern airport. The attackers used DLL side-loading with Fortemedia and SentinelOne binaries to execute malicious DLLs, leveraging tools like ChromElevator for data exfiltration. Node.js scripts were used to launch PowerShell code for reconnaissance and data staging on sendit.sh. The campaign reflects a shift towards quieter operations with improved operational hygiene. The European Council imposed sanctions on Iranian company Emennet Pasargad, linked to the IRGC-CEC, for previous cyber activities. The campaign also involved data exfiltration from organizations in the United States, Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, with some destructive operations reported.

The campaign's use of advanced techniques and infrastructure highlights the adversary's capability to conduct sophisticated cyber operations across multiple sectors and geographies.

doc_summary: In 2022, Cisco experienced a breach due to a sophisticated attack involving MFA prompt bombing. The Yanluowang ransomware group compromised a Cisco employee's personal Google account, gaining access to browser-stored credentials, including the Cisco VPN password. The attackers used repeated MFA push notifications and vishing calls to trick the employee into approving access. Once inside, they enrolled their own devices for MFA, escalated privileges, accessed Citrix servers and domain controllers, and exfiltrated 2.8GB of data. This incident highlights the vulnerabilities of push-based MFA and the need for phishing-resistant methods like FIDO2 security keys or hardware tokens. Specops Secure Access offers solutions to mitigate such risks by supporting multiple identity providers and fatigue-resistant options for Windows logon, RDP, and VPN connections. Continuous scanning of Active Directory against breached passwords and implementing conditional access policies can further enhance security.

Title: High-Severity Vulnerabilities in Angular Language Service VS Code Extension

Victim.Description: Developers using Angular Language Service VS Code extension.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves high-severity vulnerabilities in the Angular Language Service VS Code extension, exposing developers to remote code execution attacks. The vulnerabilities stem from improper input handling and insecure configuration practices, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary commands on a developer’s machine. The primary attack vectors include a JSDoc hover Markdown command injection issue and unsafe handling of the TypeScript SDK configuration. These vulnerabilities pose significant risks to developers working with Angular projects, particularly those who frequently clone repositories or install third-party packages.
doc_summary: Multiple high-severity vulnerabilities have been discovered in the Angular Language Service VS Code extension (Angular.ng-template), exposing developers to remote code execution (RCE) attacks through malicious project files and dependencies. The issues, tracked under GitHub advisory GHSA-ccq4-xmxr-8hcq, affect all versions before 21.2.4 and have been patched in the latest release. These flaws pose significant risks to developers working with Angular projects, particularly those who frequently clone repositories or install third-party packages. The vulnerabilities stem from improper input handling and insecure configuration practices within the extension, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands on a developer’s machine. One of the primary attack vectors involves a JSDoc hover Markdown command injection issue. The extension configures its Markdown renderer with a trusted mode, allowing execution of command URIs embedded in tooltips. However, the Angular Language Server fails to properly sanitize JSDoc content before rendering it. This allows attackers to embed malicious links within JSDoc comments in TypeScript or JavaScript files. When a developer hovers over a symbol and clicks the rendered link, arbitrary commands can be executed on the host system. A second critical flaw involves unsafe handling of the TypeScript SDK (tsdk) configuration within workspace settings. The extension reads tsdk-related paths directly from the .vscode/settings.json file without validating workspace trust or prompting user consent. These paths are passed to the background Node.js language server, which dynamically loads a tsserverlibrary.js file from the specified directory. An attacker can exploit this behavior by embedding a malicious tsserverlibrary.js file within a project and configuring the settings to point to it. When the workspace opens, the extension automatically loads and executes malicious code without user interaction. The combined impact of these vulnerabilities is severe, allowing full compromise of the developer’s environment. Notably, the tsdk-based attack executes silently during workspace initialization, while the JSDoc-based attack requires minimal user interaction. Both mechanisms effectively bypass VS Code’s Workspace Trust model, undermining its core security guarantees. This makes routine developer activities, such as code reviews, dependency installation, and repository cloning, potential attack vectors. The vulnerabilities are classified under multiple CWEs, including CWE-79 (cross-site scripting), CWE-94 (code injection), CWE-427 (uncontrolled search path), and CWE-494 (code download without integrity verification). The CVSS v4 score indicates high severity, with network-based attack vectors, low complexity, and no required privileges. Developers are strongly advised to immediately upgrade the Angular Language Service extension to version 21.2.4 or later. Additionally, security best practices such as reviewing workspace settings, avoiding untrusted repositories, and enabling strict workspace trust policies should be enforced. Organizations should also monitor developer environments for suspicious activity and consider restricting the execution of untrusted extensions and scripts to reduce exposure to similar supply chain-style attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves exploiting vulnerabilities in the Angular Language Service VS Code extension to achieve remote code execution. The exploitation stage is critical, with attackers leveraging JSDoc hover Markdown command injection and unsafe TypeScript SDK configuration handling. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands on a developer’s machine, bypassing VS Code’s Workspace Trust model. The attack chain highlights the importance of securing developer environments and enforcing strict workspace trust policies.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes vulnerabilities and techniques rather than specific indicators like hashes or IP addresses. The primary focus is on the exploitation of vulnerabilities in the Angular Language Service VS Code extension, specifically JSDoc hover Markdown command injection and unsafe TypeScript SDK configuration handling. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands on a developer’s machine, posing significant risks to developer environments.

Victim.Industry: Various, including consumer and enterprise sectors.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to outdated software versions.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves multiple memory safety vulnerabilities in 7-Zip 26.00, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary code and leak sensitive data. The vulnerabilities, disclosed by GitHub Security Lab, include a critical heap buffer overflow in the NTFS handler (CVE-2026-48095). The flaws affect consumer and enterprise endpoints globally, making them attractive for phishing campaigns and privilege escalation. Administrators are advised to upgrade to 7-Zip 26.01 to mitigate these risks.
doc_summary: Multiple memory safety bugs in 7-Zip 26.00 allow remote attackers to leak sensitive data and execute arbitrary code. GitHub Security Lab disclosed a critical heap buffer overflow in 7-Zip's NTFS handler (CVE-2026-48095), affecting versions up to 26.00. The NTFS handler vulnerability allows attackers to execute code by crafting malicious NTFS images. Additional vulnerabilities include out-of-bounds reads and integer overflows in formats like SquashFS and UEFI capsules. These issues impact consumer and enterprise endpoints, making them attractive for phishing campaigns and privilege escalation. Administrators should upgrade to 7-Zip 26.01 to mitigate these risks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain involves crafting malicious archive files to exploit memory safety vulnerabilities in 7-Zip 26.00. The weaponized files are delivered to victims, where they exploit the NTFS handler vulnerability (CVE-2026-48095) to execute arbitrary code. The vulnerabilities also allow data exfiltration and system compromise. The attack is facilitated by 7-Zip's format probing, which routes files to the vulnerable handler. Administrators should upgrade to 7-Zip 26.01 to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of a critical heap buffer overflow in 7-Zip's NTFS handler (CVE-2026-48095). The vulnerabilities allow remote code execution and data leakage, making them significant threats. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains limits the ability to detect and respond to the attack. Administrators should focus on upgrading to 7-Zip 26.01 and monitoring for suspicious archive file activity.

Title: ConnectWise Automate RMM Platform Vulnerability CVE-2026-9089

Victim.Description: Managed service providers using ConnectWise Automate RMM platform.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a high-severity vulnerability in the ConnectWise Automate RMM platform, tracked as CVE-2026-9089. The vulnerability allows attackers to bypass integrity verification mechanisms, potentially enabling unauthorized code execution. The flaw exists in the agent's plugin loading and self-update processes, posing a significant risk to managed service providers using the platform. ConnectWise has addressed the issue in version 2026.5, emphasizing the importance of timely patch management and robust validation mechanisms.
doc_summary: ConnectWise has released a security update to address a high-severity vulnerability in its ConnectWise Automate remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, tracked as CVE-2026-9089. This flaw, with a CVSS score of 8.8, allows attackers to bypass integrity verification mechanisms, potentially enabling unauthorized code execution. The vulnerability exists in the agent's plugin loading and self-update processes, falling under CWE-494. Successful exploitation could lead to arbitrary code execution, system integrity compromise, and persistent network access. The centralized nature of RMM tools poses a broader supply chain risk, especially for MSPs managing multiple client infrastructures. ConnectWise resolved the issue in Automate version 2026.5 by enhancing integrity verification. Users are advised to apply the patch within 30 days and take additional precautions like monitoring agent activity and deploying EDR solutions.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation of a vulnerability in the ConnectWise Automate RMM platform, allowing attackers to bypass integrity verification mechanisms. This exploitation could lead to unauthorized code execution, compromising system integrity and potentially providing persistent access across networks. The vulnerability requires no user interaction and has low attack complexity, increasing its potential impact. ConnectWise has released a patch to address the issue, highlighting the need for timely updates and monitoring for unusual activity.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the vulnerability CVE-2026-9089, which allows attackers to bypass integrity verification mechanisms in the ConnectWise Automate RMM platform. No specific indicators such as hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The focus is on the exploitation technique and the need for robust validation mechanisms and timely patch management to mitigate the risk.

Title: Apache CXF LDAP Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-44930

Victim.Description: Organizations using vulnerable versions of Apache CXF with the XKMS service.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in Apache CXF's XKMS service, allowing LDAP injection attacks. The adversary can manipulate LDAP queries to access sensitive certificate data, impacting systems relying on certificate-based authentication. The capability is centered around exploiting CVE-2026-44930, with the infrastructure being Apache CXF systems using the XKMS service. Victims are organizations using vulnerable Apache CXF versions.
doc_summary: Apache CXF users face a significant security risk due to a newly disclosed vulnerability, CVE-2026-44930, which exposes systems to LDAP injection attacks. This vulnerability affects the LDAP certificate repository within the XKMS service of Apache CXF, specifically in the cxf-services-xkms-x509-repo-ldap component. Improper input validation allows attackers to manipulate LDAP queries, potentially retrieving arbitrary certificates and bypassing access controls. The flaw impacts multiple Apache CXF versions, including 4.2.0 before 4.2.1, 4.0.0 before 4.1.6, and all versions before 3.6.11. Apache has released patches in versions 4.2.1, 4.1.6, and 3.6.11. Organizations are urged to upgrade immediately and review their LDAP query-handling mechanisms. The vulnerability was disclosed via the Apache CXF developer mailing list, highlighting the ongoing risk of injection vulnerabilities and the importance of secure coding practices.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves exploiting an LDAP injection vulnerability in Apache CXF's XKMS service. The exploitation stage is critical, where attackers manipulate LDAP queries to access sensitive certificate data. Actions on objectives include unauthorized access to certificate repositories. Detection involves monitoring LDAP query logs, while remediation includes upgrading to patched versions and implementing input validation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs related to LDAP injection attacks. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified. The focus is on detecting LDAP query manipulation and unauthorized access to certificate data. Remediation involves upgrading Apache CXF to patched versions and enforcing input validation.

doc_summary: The Iranian state-sponsored threat actor Nimbus Manticore, affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, launched a campaign targeting the aviation and software sectors in the United States, Europe, and the Middle East. The campaign involved AI-assisted development of a new backdoor, MiniFast, and employed techniques such as AppDomain hijacking and SEO poisoning. The threat actor used phishing lures impersonating organizations and distributed trojanized software installers. The campaign was active from February to April 2026, with attacks on entities in Saudi Arabia, Australia, and the United States. The MiniFast backdoor supports remote command execution and persistence mechanisms, indicating a high level of sophistication and strategic objectives beyond espionage.
kill_chain_summary: The campaign followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization with AI-assisted malware development. Delivery was achieved through phishing and trojanized software, leading to exploitation via AppDomain hijacking. Installation of the MiniFast backdoor enabled command and control, culminating in data exfiltration.

Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to hard-coded machine keys

diamond_model_summary: The incident involved an unknown adversary exploiting CVE-2026-5426 in the Digital Knowledge KnowledgeDeliver LMS. The adversary used Godzilla web shell and Cobalt Strike Beacon to gain and maintain access. The infrastructure included compromised LMS systems, and the victims were primarily in the education sector in Japan. The attack highlighted the risks of shared secrets in deployment templates.
doc_summary: A high-severity security flaw, CVE-2026-5426, in Digital Knowledge KnowledgeDeliver LMS was exploited as a zero-day vulnerability. The flaw, due to hard-coded ASP.NET machine keys, allowed unauthenticated remote code execution via ViewState deserialization. Attackers deployed the Godzilla web shell and Cobalt Strike Beacon, targeting users of the LMS. The vulnerability affected installations before February 24, 2026, and similar issues were noted in Sitecore Experience Manager and Gladinet CentreStack. The attack involved injecting malicious code, escalating file system access, and tricking users into downloading a fake security plugin. The payloads were tailored using the compromised organization's name, highlighting the risks of shared secrets in deployment templates.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the exploitation of CVE-2026-5426, allowing remote code execution via ViewState deserialization. The adversary delivered malicious payloads using HTTP requests, installed the Godzilla web shell for persistence, and used Cobalt Strike Beacon for command and control. Actions on objectives included privilege escalation and user deception through JavaScript tampering.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of Godzilla web shell and Cobalt Strike Beacon as tools, with TTPs involving ViewState deserialization and exploitation of CVE-2026-5426.
