The infrastructure involves compromised LMS installations, and the victims are organizations using vulnerable KnowledgeDeliver deployments. The attack highlights the risks of shared cryptographic secrets.
doc_summary: Hackers are exploiting a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-5426, in the KnowledgeDeliver Learning Management System (LMS) to deploy the BLUEBEAM web shell. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution through ASP.NET ViewState deserialization. The vulnerability affects installations before February 24, 2026, using hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values. Attackers can craft malicious ViewState payloads to execute arbitrary code. Mandiant's Google Threat Intelligence Group observed this in real-world attacks. Post-exploitation, attackers deployed BLUEBEAM, a .NET-based in-memory web shell, and modified file permissions using icacls. They injected malicious JavaScript to display fake security alerts and installed a fraudulent authentication plugin, leading to Cobalt Strike BEACON backdoor infections. Organizations should monitor Windows Application logs for Event ID 1316 and suspicious processes spawned by w3wp.exe. Mitigation includes rotating ASP.NET machine keys, restricting access to trusted IP ranges, and implementing file integrity monitoring.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2026-5426, allowing threat actors to execute remote code via ASP.NET ViewState deserialization. The weaponization involves crafting malicious ViewState payloads, delivered through the __VIEWSTATE parameter. Post-exploitation, the BLUEBEAM web shell is installed in-memory, enabling command and control via encrypted HTTP POST requests. Actions on objectives include modifying file permissions and injecting malicious JavaScript to deceive users.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of BLUEBEAM and Cobalt Strike BEACON malware, exploiting CVE-2026-5426. The adversary employs in-memory execution and encrypted HTTP POST requests for command and control. The use of shared ASP.NET machineKey values poses a significant risk, as it allows attackers to target multiple environments. Detection is challenging due to the in-memory nature of the malware and the modification of file permissions.

Title: Kali365 PhaaS Platform Exploits OAuth Device Code Authentication

Victim.Description: Organizations using Microsoft 365, targeted through phishing campaigns.

diamond_model_summary: The Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform is used by cybercriminals, including the ShinyHunters group, to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts. The platform exploits OAuth device code authentication to bypass multi-factor authentication, allowing attackers to steal session tokens and gain unauthorized access. Kali365 provides low-skilled attackers with advanced phishing capabilities, including AI-generated lures and real-time victim-tracking dashboards. The platform operates as a business with admins, resellers, and affiliates, and is distributed via Telegram channels. Victims are primarily organizations using Microsoft 365, targeted through phishing emails that direct them to Microsoft's device code login portal.
doc_summary: The FBI has issued a warning about the Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform, which emerged in April 2026. This platform is used to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts by exploiting OAuth device code authentication, allowing attackers to steal session tokens and bypass multi-factor authentication. Distributed via Telegram channels, Kali365 enables cybercriminals to compromise accounts without stealing passwords or intercepting MFA codes. The platform uses device code phishing, a method that abuses Microsoft Entra and Microsoft 365 accounts. Extortion gangs, including the ShinyHunters, have targeted Microsoft Entra accounts using device-code and voice phishing. Attackers initiate the device authorization process to generate a code, tricking targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page. Once the victim completes MFA, an OAuth access token is issued, granting full access to the account. Kali365 provides low-skilled attackers with advanced phishing capabilities, including AI-generated lures and real-time victim-tracking dashboards. Security researchers reported widespread campaigns targeting Microsoft 365 environments, where attackers created malicious inbox rules and registered new devices. The FBI recommends restricting device code authentication flows and auditing existing usage.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where attackers identify targets using phishing emails. During weaponization, phishing lures and campaign templates are created. Delivery involves sending phishing emails that direct victims to Microsoft's device code login portal. Exploitation occurs when victims unknowingly authorize attackers to access their accounts. Installation involves creating malicious inbox rules and registering new devices. Command and control is maintained using OAuth tokens, allowing attackers to access and exfiltrate data from compromised accounts. The FBI recommends restricting device code authentication flows and auditing existing usage to mitigate these attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names such as microsoft.com, which are used in phishing campaigns. The attack leverages OAuth device code authentication as a tool to bypass multi-factor authentication. Tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) include device code phishing and adversary-in-the-middle attacks. The lack of specific hash values, IP addresses, and network host artifacts limits the ability to provide a comprehensive Pyramid of Pain analysis. Organizations are advised to implement Conditional Access policies and monitor for suspicious activity to detect and mitigate these attacks.

diamond_model_summary: The GitHub breach via the Nx Console VS Code extension highlights a sophisticated supply chain attack by TeamPCP. The adversary leveraged a compromised developer tool to exfiltrate repositories, impacting multiple companies. This incident underscores the evolving threat landscape in software supply chains.
doc_summary: GitHub confirmed a breach of its internal repositories due to a compromised employee device involving a poisoned version of the Nx Console VS Code extension. doc_summary: NGINX users face a critical security issue due to a vulnerability, CVE-2026-9256, in the ngx_http_rewrite_module. Dubbed 'Nginx-poolslip', this flaw allows denial-of-service (DoS) and potential remote code execution (RCE) through improper handling of overlapping PCRE capture groups. The vulnerability affects NGINX Open Source versions 1.0.0 to 1.30.1 and NGINX Plus version 37.0.0, with fixes in versions 1.30.2, 1.31.1, and 37.0.1.1. Exploitation involves sending crafted HTTP requests, leading to heap-based buffer overflow (CWE-122). The vulnerability, disclosed by Mufeed VH, Nebula Security, and Vexera AI, has a CVSS v3.1 score of 8.1 and v4.0 score of 9.2. Affected products include NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX App Protect, and NGINX Gateway Fabric. F5 products like BIG-IP and BIG-IQ are not affected. Organizations are advised to patch immediately, audit rewrite rules, and enable mitigations like ASLR.

The attacks involve stealing admin API keys, injecting malicious JavaScript, and using a lightweight loader to fetch second-stage code. This code fingerprints visitors and serves a fake Cloudflare prompt, leading to payload execution. Multiple payloads, including DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers, and an Electron-based malware sample named UtilifySetup.exe, have been observed. Administrators are urged to upgrade to Ghost CMS version 6.19.1 or later and rotate all keys. XLab provided indicators of compromise for thorough website reviews.

Title: Supply Chain Attack on Laravel Lang Packages via GitHub Tags

Victim.Description: Developers using Laravel Lang localization packages were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The attack on Laravel Lang packages involved a sophisticated adversary exploiting GitHub version tags to distribute credential-stealing malware. The adversary's capability included manipulating tags to disguise malicious commits, leveraging Composer for delivery, and using a C2 server at flipboxstudio.info. Victims were developers using Laravel Lang packages, with data types at risk including cloud credentials and SSH keys.
doc_summary: A sophisticated supply chain attack targeted Laravel Lang localization packages, exploiting GitHub version tags to distribute credential-stealing malware via Composer. Attackers rewrote tags in four repositories, affecting laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, and possibly laravel-lang/actions. The attack involved a malicious 'src/helpers.php' file acting as a dropper, downloading a cross-platform credential stealer from flipboxstudio.info. The malware harvested cloud credentials, Kubernetes secrets, Vault tokens, Git credentials, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, password managers, VPN configurations, and local .env files. On Windows, it extracted a base64-encoded executable targeting Chrome, Brave, and Edge. The incident was reported to Packagist, which removed malicious versions and unlisted affected packages. Developers are advised to review package versions, rotate credentials, and check for connections to flipboxstudio.info.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain: reconnaissance to identify target repositories, weaponization by creating malicious payloads, delivery through Composer package installations, exploitation via execution of malicious code, installation of the payload, command and control communication with flipboxstudio.info, and actions on objectives by harvesting credentials and sensitive data.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like flipboxstudio.info, which are challenging for adversaries to change. The use of specific tools like Composer and TTPs such as supply chain attacks and credential theft are also significant indicators. These elements contribute to a higher level of difficulty for the adversary to adapt if detected.

Title: Coordinated Supply Chain Attack on Packagist Packages

Victim.Description: The attack targeted software development projects using Packagist Composer packages.

diamond_model_summary: The attack involved a coordinated supply chain compromise targeting Packagist packages. The adversary inserted malicious code into package.json files, exploiting cross-ecosystem placement to execute a Linux binary. The attack leveraged GitHub Releases for hosting the payload, indicating a sophisticated approach. The victim sector is software development, with a high impact severity due to the potential for remote code execution and data exfiltration.
doc_summary: A coordinated supply chain attack targeted eight Packagist packages, inserting malicious code into package.json files. The attack involved downloading a Linux binary from a GitHub Releases URL, saving it to /tmp/.sshd, and executing it. The attack exploited cross-ecosystem placement, affecting projects with JavaScript and PHP code. The malicious code was found in 777 GitHub files, indicating a broader campaign. The GitHub account hosting the payload is unavailable, and the malware, named gvfsd-network, mimics a GNOME Virtual File System daemon. The attack provides remote code execution and disables TLS verification. The severity is high, and the attack impacts software development and security sectors.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of package.json files to include malicious scripts. Delivery occurred through compromised Packagist packages, leading to the installation of a Linux binary. The binary executed in the background, potentially establishing a command and control channel. The attack aimed to execute malicious binaries and exfiltrate data, highlighting the need for robust supply chain security measures.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The attack's indicators include the domain github.com and the malware family gvfsd-network. The adversary's use of GitHub Releases for hosting the payload and the cross-ecosystem targeting strategy complicate detection and response efforts. The attack's sophistication is evident in its ability to bypass traditional security measures, emphasizing the importance of monitoring supply chain dependencies and implementing robust detection mechanisms.

Title: Dismantling of CINEMAGOAL Piracy Ecosystem by Italian Authorities

Victim.Description: Streaming platforms like Netflix, Disney+, and Spotify, and their legitimate subscribers.

diamond_model_summary: The CINEMAGOAL piracy ecosystem was dismantled by Italian authorities. The adversary, CINEMAGOAL operators, used advanced capabilities to provide unauthorized access to streaming services. Their infrastructure included servers in France and Germany, and virtual machines in Italy. Victims were major streaming platforms and their legitimate subscribers.
doc_summary: Italian authorities dismantled the CINEMAGOAL piracy ecosystem, which provided illegal access to streaming platforms like Netflix, Disney+, and Spotify. The operation, named Tutto Chiaro, involved 100 searches across Italy, seizing materials to identify involved individuals and illegal profits. CINEMAGOAL used an app to connect to legitimate platforms, fetching decryption codes from foreign servers. The system used virtual machines in Italy to capture and redistribute authentication codes. The operation was coordinated by Eurojust, with servers seized in France and Germany. The illegal business had over 70 resellers, causing damages of around €300 million. Authorities are analyzing seized materials to identify all parties involved.
kill_chain_summary: The CINEMAGOAL operation involved multiple stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Reconnaissance was conducted to gather information on streaming platforms. Weaponization involved developing the CINEMAGOAL app. Delivery was achieved by distributing the app to customers. Exploitation involved using valid decryption codes. Installation occurred on customer devices. Command and Control was maintained through foreign servers. Actions on Objectives included providing unauthorized streaming services.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the CINEMAGOAL incident includes various indicators. Hash values and IP addresses were not specifically identified. Domain names and network host artifacts were part of the infrastructure. Tools included virtual machines and decryption tools. TTPs involved IP address masking and unauthorized access to streaming services. The scoring reflects the complexity of disrupting these indicators.

Title: Project Glasswing Uncovers Critical Vulnerabilities in Global Software

Victim.Description: Global software projects affected by vulnerabilities

diamond_model_summary: Project Glasswing, led by Anthropic, utilized the Claude Mythos Preview AI model to identify over 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in globally important software. The initiative involved 50 partners and focused on open-source projects, with 1,726 vulnerabilities confirmed as true positives. A critical flaw in WolfSSL (CVE-2026-5194) was among the findings, allowing certificate forgery. The project resulted in 97 patches and 88 advisories, highlighting the challenge of fixing vulnerabilities. Anthropic emphasizes the need for faster patch cycles and improved cyber defenses as AI models like Mythos Preview become more available.
doc_summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing has identified over 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in globally important software since its launch. The initiative, involving 50 partners, uses the Claude Mythos Preview AI model to detect vulnerabilities, with 1,726 confirmed as true positives. A critical flaw in WolfSSL (CVE-2026-5194) was among the findings, allowing certificate forgery. The project has led to 97 patches and 88 advisories. Anthropic emphasizes the challenge of fixing vulnerabilities and urges faster patch cycles. The AI model also helped prevent a $1.5 million fraud attempt. Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program allows security professionals to use its models for legitimate purposes. The company highlights the need for improved cyber defenses as AI models like Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5-Cyber become more available.
kill_chain_summary: The incident involves the use of the Claude Mythos Preview AI model to conduct reconnaissance and identify vulnerabilities in software. The model actively scanned for vulnerabilities, leading to the exploitation of identified weaknesses, such as the critical flaw in WolfSSL (CVE-2026-5194). The exploitation stage involved gaining initial access through public-facing applications. The incident highlights the importance of addressing vulnerabilities promptly and improving patch cycles to mitigate risks. Anthropic's initiative underscores the potential of AI in enhancing cybersecurity defenses and the need for organizations to adapt to AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of the Claude Mythos Preview AI model as a tool for identifying vulnerabilities. The critical vulnerability CVE-2026-5194 in WolfSSL represents a significant threat, emphasizing the need for effective detection and remediation strategies. While specific hashes, IP addresses, and domains were not identified, the incident highlights the importance of addressing vulnerabilities at the TTP level to disrupt adversary operations. The use of AI models in vulnerability discovery presents both opportunities and challenges for cybersecurity, necessitating robust defenses and timely patching to mitigate risks.

diamond_model_summary: The attack on Laravel-Lang PHP packages represents a sophisticated supply chain compromise. doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a supply chain attack targeting Laravel-Lang PHP packages. The attack involves a credential-stealing framework embedded in over 700 versions of the packages, indicating a compromise of the Laravel Lang organization's release process. The malicious code is located in 'src/helpers.php' and contacts an external server 'flipboxstudio.info' to retrieve a cross-platform payload. The payload executes a Visual Basic Script launcher on Windows and a stealer payload on Linux and macOS. The malware collects data, encrypts it with AES-256, and exfiltrates it to 'flipboxstudio.info/exfil'. The attack is suspected to involve access to organization-level credentials or release infrastructure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance on the Laravel-Lang release process. The adversary weaponized PHP packages with a credential-stealing framework, delivering them through the compromised repository. The malicious code exploits the autoload feature in PHP applications, installing the stealer and establishing command and control with a C2 server. The malware collects credentials and exfiltrates them, demonstrating a complete attack lifecycle from initial access to data exfiltration.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names and network host artifacts as key indicators. The domain 'flipboxstudio.info' serves as the C2 server, while the malicious file 'src/helpers.php' is a critical artifact. The use of a credential-stealing framework and the compromise of PHP packages highlight the need for robust monitoring and validation of software supply chains.

doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-48172, with a CVSS score of 10.0, has been identified in the LiteSpeed User-End cPanel Plugin. This flaw allows attackers to exploit incorrect privilege assignments to execute arbitrary scripts with root permissions. The vulnerability affects plugin versions 2.3 to 2.4.4, with a patch available in version 2.4.5. Security researcher David Strydom discovered the flaw, which is actively exploited in the wild. LiteSpeed has released updates for both cPanel and WHM plugins to address this and other potential attack vectors. Users are advised to upgrade to the latest versions or remove the vulnerable plugin if immediate patching is not possible. The incident highlights the importance of timely security updates in the web hosting industry.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident primarily involves the exploitation stage, where attackers leverage CVE-2026-48172 to gain elevated privileges on affected cPanel servers. The exploitation allows for arbitrary script execution as root, posing significant risks to server integrity and data security. Detection involves monitoring for unusual script execution and unauthorized access attempts. Remediation includes upgrading to patched plugin versions or removing the vulnerable plugin if immediate patching is not feasible. The incident highlights the criticality of addressing privilege escalation vulnerabilities promptly.

Title: Ghostwriter Campaign Targeting Ukrainian Government via Prometheus Lures

Victim.Description: Ukrainian government organizations targeted via phishing.

diamond_model_summary: The Ghostwriter campaign targeting Ukrainian government entities is characterized by the use of phishing emails with Prometheus-related lures. The adversary employs sophisticated malware, including OYSTERFRESH and OYSTERBLUES, to gain persistence and exfiltrate data. The infrastructure involves C2 communication over HTTP, and the victims are primarily government organizations in Ukraine.
doc_summary: The Belarus-aligned threat actor known as Ghostwriter, also referred to as UAC-0057 and UNC1151, has been targeting Ukrainian government organizations using phishing emails. These emails exploit lures related to Prometheus, a Ukrainian online learning platform. The campaign, active since spring 2026, involves sending emails with PDF attachments that link to a ZIP archive containing a JavaScript file named OYSTERFRESH. This file displays a decoy document while writing an encrypted payload called OYSTERBLUES to the Windows Registry and downloading OYSTERSHUCK to decode it. OYSTERBLUES collects system information and communicates with a C2 server. The final payload is Cobalt Strike, used for post-exploitation. CERT-UA advises restricting wscript.exe execution for standard users. The campaign is part of broader cyber activities involving AI tools by Russia for intelligence gathering and influence operations.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance and weaponization, where malicious PDFs and JavaScript files are prepared. Delivery occurs via phishing emails targeting Ukrainian government entities. doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has identified a critical vulnerability in Langflow, tracked as CVE-2025-34291, due to an origin validation flaw. This vulnerability, classified under CWE-346, arises from an overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) configuration and insecure cookie settings, allowing refresh token cookies to be sent in cross-origin requests. Organizations using Langflow are urged to apply security patches, restrict CORS policies, and configure cookies with secure attributes. Victim.Description: Organizations using Trend Micro Apex One on-premise deployments.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-34926, a directory traversal vulnerability in Trend Micro Apex One. The adversary's capability includes manipulating server-side files to inject malicious code, turning the security platform into a malware delivery mechanism. The infrastructure targeted includes on-premise deployments of Trend Micro Apex One, affecting various industries globally. The victim's security posture is vulnerable, with a critical impact severity due to the potential for full network compromise.
doc_summary: CISA has added a newly disclosed vulnerability in Trend Micro Apex One to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, warning that the flaw is actively being exploited in real-world attacks. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-34926, affects on-premise deployments of Trend Micro Apex One and poses a significant risk to enterprise environments. The vulnerability is classified as a directory traversal flaw (CWE-23) that allows a pre-authenticated local attacker to manipulate server-side files. Specifically, the flaw enables attackers to modify a critical key table within the Apex One server. By exploiting this weakness, threat actors can inject malicious code that is subsequently distributed to connected endpoint agents, effectively turning the security platform into a delivery mechanism for malware. According to CISA, the vulnerability was added to the KEV catalog on May 21, 2026, highlighting confirmed evidence of active exploitation. While there are currently no public reports directly linking the flaw to ransomware campaigns, the potential for large-scale compromise makes it particularly dangerous. Attackers leveraging this vulnerability could gain widespread access across enterprise networks by abusing trusted update mechanisms. Trend Micro Apex One is widely used for endpoint protection, making it a high-value target for adversaries. The ability to inject malicious payloads into agents managed by the platform significantly amplifies the impact of exploitation, potentially leading to full network compromise, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. CISA has issued a directive requiring federal agencies to remediate the vulnerability by June 4, 2026. The agency strongly urges organizations to immediately follow vendor-provided mitigation guidance.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain stages identified in this incident include exploitation of the CVE-2026-34926 vulnerability, allowing adversaries to manipulate server-side files and inject malicious code into endpoint agents. This leads to potential installation of unauthorized code and actions on objectives such as full network compromise, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. Detection focuses on monitoring for unusual modifications and agent behavior, while remediation involves applying patches and restricting access.

Title: Showboat Linux Malware Campaign Targeting Middle Eastern Telecommunications

Victim.Description: Telecommunications provider in the Middle East targeted by Showboat malware.

diamond_model_summary: The Showboat malware campaign is attributed to China-affiliated threat clusters targeting the telecommunications sector in the Middle East. The adversary employs sophisticated capabilities, including a modular post-exploitation framework with SOCKS5 proxy functionality. The infrastructure involves Chengdu-based C2 nodes, and victims include telecommunications providers in the Middle East, with potential compromises in Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, the United States, and Ukraine.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified a new Linux malware named Showboat, targeting a telecommunications provider in the Middle East since mid-2022. Showboat is a modular post-exploitation framework capable of remote shell spawning, file transfer, and SOCKS5 proxy functionality. The malware is linked to China-affiliated threat clusters, with C2 nodes geolocated to Chengdu, Sichuan. Showboat shares similarities with other frameworks like PlugX and ShadowPad, indicating a digital quartermaster's involvement. The investigation began with an ELF binary uploaded to VirusTotal in May 2025, classified as a sophisticated Linux backdoor with rootkit-like capabilities, tracked by Kaspersky as EvaRAT. Showboat contacts a C2 server, gathers system information, and transmits it as an encrypted Base64-encoded string. It can upload/download files, conceal its presence, and manage C2 servers. The malware retrieves a code snippet from Pastebin for stealth and scans for devices via SOCKS5 proxy. Victims include an ISP in Afghanistan and an unknown entity in Azerbaijan, with possible compromises in the United States and Ukraine.
kill_chain_summary: The Showboat malware campaign involves several stages of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. Installation is achieved through the deployment of a rootkit-like backdoor on compromised systems. Command and Control is established via a SOCKS5 proxy, allowing communication with Chengdu-based C2 servers. Actions on Objectives include data exfiltration and lateral movement within the targeted telecommunications infrastructure.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the Showboat malware campaign includes several indicators. Hash values of the malware samples provide a basic level of detection. IP addresses associated with Chengdu-based C2 nodes offer a more challenging detection opportunity. The use of SOCKS5 proxy and rootkit-like capabilities represent higher levels of pain for adversaries, as they require more sophisticated detection and remediation efforts.

Title: Apache OFBiz Authentication Bypass and RCE Vulnerability

Victim.Description: Organizations using Apache OFBiz versions before 24.09.06.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in Apache OFBiz, allowing attackers to bypass authentication and execute remote code. The adversary exploits flaws in the LoginWorker.checkLogin() method and ProgramExport.groovy script. The capability includes exploiting CVE-2026-45434 for remote code execution. The infrastructure consists of vulnerable Apache OFBiz instances. Victims are organizations using affected versions of Apache OFBiz.
doc_summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Apache OFBiz allows attackers to hijack forced password-change flows and achieve remote code execution (RCE) via a single HTTP request, affecting all versions before 24.09.06. The vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-45434, was discovered by researchers at Aretiq AI. It involves flaws in the LoginWorker.checkLogin() method and the ProgramExport.groovy script, allowing attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability is similar to CVE-2023-51467 and affects all versions of Apache OFBiz before 24.09.06, including the entire 18.12.x branch and 24.09.x through 24.09.05. Apache addressed the issue in version 24.09.06 with three commits that remove the client-controlled requirePasswordChange parameter, add permission checks, and introduce a Groovy sandbox. Immediate mitigation steps include upgrading to Apache OFBiz 24.09.06, removing or changing default passwords for demo accounts, and restricting access to vulnerable endpoints.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with exploiting authentication bypass and RCE vulnerabilities in Apache OFBiz. The adversary gains initial access by exploiting public-facing applications and using valid accounts. The exploitation stage involves bypassing authentication and executing arbitrary code. The actions on objectives stage includes executing commands on the compromised system. Detection involves monitoring specific HTTP POST requests, and remediation includes upgrading to a patched version and securing demo accounts.

Title: NGINX Zero-Day Vulnerability 'nginx-poolslip' Exposes Servers to RCE

Victim.Description: Victims are organizations using NGINX version 1.31.0, including web servers, reverse proxies, load balancers, and API gateways.

diamond_model_summary: The 'nginx-poolslip' zero-day vulnerability represents a critical threat to NGINX servers globally. Discovered by the NebSec team, this vulnerability allows remote code execution by bypassing ASLR protections. The adversary, likely sophisticated, exploits this flaw to compromise systems. Organizations using NGINX version 1.31.0 are at risk, necessitating immediate security measures.
doc_summary: A newly discovered zero-day vulnerability in NGINX, named 'nginx-poolslip', poses a critical threat by exposing millions of servers to potential remote code execution (RCE) attacks. This vulnerability affects NGINX version 1.31.0, the latest stable release, and was discovered by security researcher Vega from the NebSec team. Publicly disclosed on May 21, 2026, the flaw resides in NGINX's internal memory pool management mechanism and can bypass Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a key operating system protection. This vulnerability follows the recent CVE-2026-42945, a critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the ngx_http_rewrite_module. Despite patches for previous vulnerabilities, the nginx-poolslip effectively bypasses mitigations, leaving even fully updated systems at risk. No official CVE identifier has been assigned yet, and neither F5 nor the NGINX project has released a patch. Organizations are advised to monitor NebSec and F5 security advisories, restrict exposure of NGINX administrative interfaces, deploy Web Application Firewall (WAF) rules, ensure ASLR is fully enabled, and consider alternative architectures for critical environments.
kill_chain_summary: The 'nginx-poolslip' vulnerability primarily affects the exploitation stage of the MITRE ATT&CK kill chain. By exploiting this zero-day in NGINX's memory pool management, attackers can achieve remote code execution. The vulnerability bypasses ASLR, a critical defense mechanism, allowing adversaries to execute malicious payloads reliably. Organizations must monitor for unusual activity and apply mitigations.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The 'nginx-poolslip' vulnerability presents a significant challenge in the Pyramid of Pain. The primary focus is on the TTPs, particularly the ASLR bypass technique, which requires advanced detection and mitigation strategies. Organizations must prioritize monitoring and patching efforts.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a vulnerability in the Linux kernel, CVE-2026-46333, which allows local privilege escalation. The adversary can exploit this vulnerability to gain root access and disclose sensitive files. The capability involves exploiting the __ptrace_may_access() function, affecting major Linux distributions. The infrastructure is not specified, but the victim includes systems running Debian, Fedora, and Ubuntu. The impact is medium, with potential exposure of sensitive credential material.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a vulnerability in the Linux kernel, tracked as CVE-2026-46333, with a CVSS score of 5.5. This vulnerability, named ssh-keysign-pwn, involves improper privilege management, allowing unprivileged local users to disclose sensitive files and execute arbitrary commands as root on default installations of major distributions like Debian, Fedora, and Ubuntu. Discovered by Qualys, the flaw is rooted in the kernel's __ptrace_may_access() function, introduced in November 2016. Exploitation could permit attackers to disclose /etc/shadow and host private keys under /etc/ssh/*_key, and execute commands as root through exploits targeting chage, ssh-keysign, pkexec, and accounts-daemon. A proof-of-concept exploit was released shortly after a public kernel commit. The vulnerability follows other recent Linux kernel vulnerabilities like Copy Fail, Dirty Frag, and Fragnesia. Users are advised to apply the latest kernel updates or use temporary workarounds like raising kernel.yama.ptrace_scope to 2. Qualys recommends rotating host keys and reviewing administrative material on affected hosts.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves exploitation of the CVE-2026-46333 vulnerability in the Linux kernel. The adversary gains initial access through local exploitation, leading to privilege escalation. Actions on objectives include disclosing sensitive files and executing arbitrary commands as root. doc_summary: CVE-2026-46333 is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability affecting SSH private keys and sensitive credentials. Present since 2016, it allows local attackers to escalate privileges from a basic shell account to full root access on popular Linux distributions like Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora. The flaw exploits the ptrace mechanism, allowing attackers to access privileged processes during a brief timing window. This can lead to the theft of SSH host private keys, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks and compromising remote trust relationships. The vulnerability affects Linux versions since 4.10-rc1 and has been confirmed exploitable on default installations of Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, and Fedora 43 and 44. An upstream fix has been released, and admins are advised to patch systems and rotate exposed credentials. Temporary mitigation includes setting kernel.yama.ptrace_scope to 2, though this may impact debugging tools.

doc_summary: A recently patched Linux privilege escalation vulnerability, named PinTheft by the V12 security team, has a publicly available proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit. This vulnerability exists in the Linux kernel's RDS (Reliable Datagram Sockets) and affects Arch Linux systems. The exploit leverages an RDS zerocopy double-free that can be turned into a page-cache overwrite through io_uring fixed buffers. The bug resides in the RDS zerocopy send path, where rds_message_zcopy_from_user() pins user pages. If a page faults, the error path drops the pages, and later RDS message cleanup drops them again. The PoC exploit steals FOLL_PIN references until io_uring holds a stolen page pointer, allowing root shell access. Successful exploitation requires the RDS module, io_uring API, a readable SUID-root binary, and x86_64 support. The RDS module is enabled by default only on Arch Linux among common distros. Users are advised to install the latest kernel updates or use mitigations to block exploitation attempts.

Title: Shai-Hulud Worm Compromises Trust Wallet Extension

Victim.Description: Trust Wallet users were targeted through a compromised Chrome extension.

diamond_model_summary: The Shai-Hulud incident involved a sophisticated adversary using a self-replicating npm worm to compromise Trust Wallet users. The adversary's capability included deploying a trojanized Chrome extension to capture seed phrases. The infrastructure leveraged AI-generated lookalike domains, and the victims were primarily cryptocurrency users. The attack highlights the need for runtime behavioral monitoring.
doc_summary: In December 2025, a self-replicating npm worm named Shai-Hulud compromised Trust Wallet users by harvesting developer credentials and pushing a trojanized Chrome extension. The attack leveraged AI-generated lookalike domains and browser-runtime abuse, resulting in $8.5 million in losses. The malicious extension captured seed phrases and transmitted them to a disguised domain. The incident highlights the need for runtime behavioral monitoring and the limitations of static analysis and traditional security controls. The attack also involved phishing campaigns targeting JavaScript libraries, leading to widespread code injection and data exfiltration.
kill_chain_summary: The Shai-Hulud attack followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to identify target npm packages. Weaponization involved creating a trojanized Chrome extension, which was delivered through the official Chrome Web Store. Exploitation occurred as the extension captured seed phrases, and installation was achieved by users unknowingly installing the extension. Command and control were established via a lookalike domain, leading to the final objective of draining cryptocurrency wallets.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Shai-Hulud incident presents challenges across the Pyramid of Pain. Hash values and IP addresses were not explicitly identified, but domain names like trustwallet-analytics.com were crucial. The use of AI-generated domains and browser-runtime abuse tools increased the difficulty of detection. The TTPs employed, such as credential harvesting and supply chain compromise, highlight the need for advanced detection capabilities.

Title: Critical Vulnerability in FreePBX User Control Panel

Victim.Description: Organizations using FreePBX for voice communications

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in FreePBX, allowing unauthenticated attackers to exploit hard-coded credentials in the User Control Panel. The adversary can gain unauthorized access to sensitive user data, impacting confidentiality and integrity. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-46376, affects FreePBX versions 16 and 17, and requires immediate patching to mitigate the risk.
doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-46376, has been identified in FreePBX, an open-source PBX platform. This flaw affects the User Control Panel (UCP) via the 'userman' module, allowing unauthenticated attackers to access user portals. The vulnerability, classified as CWE-798, arises from hard-coded credentials used during the UCP template setup process. If administrators do not change these default credentials, attackers can exploit them to gain unauthorized access, impacting confidentiality and integrity. The issue affects FreePBX versions 16 before 16.0.45 and 17 before 17.0.7. Patched versions have been released, and users are urged to update immediately. The vulnerability was reported by researcher s0nnyWT and coordinated by FreePBX maintainers, with remediation developed by Sangoma. Security experts recommend auditing deployments for weak credentials and reviewing access logs for suspicious activity. Organizations using FreePBX should prioritize patching and secure configuration to prevent unauthorized access and data exposure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack chain begins with reconnaissance, where attackers scan for FreePBX instances with default credentials. Exploitation occurs through the use of hard-coded credentials, allowing unauthorized access to the User Control Panel. The final stage involves actions on objectives, where attackers access sensitive user data. Mitigation includes updating the 'userman' module and changing default credentials.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of hard-coded credentials, a significant weakness that attackers can leverage with low complexity. No specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains were identified, but the focus is on the vulnerability itself and the need for patching and secure configuration to prevent unauthorized access.

Title: High-Severity Vulnerability in NGINX JavaScript Module (CVE-2026-8711)

Victim.Description: Organizations using NGINX JavaScript module versions 0.9.4 through 0.9.8 with vulnerable configurations.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a high-severity vulnerability in the NGINX JavaScript module, allowing remote attackers to crash servers and potentially execute arbitrary code. The vulnerability is a heap-based buffer overflow, specifically when the js_fetch_proxy directive is used with client-controlled variables and ngx.fetch() calls. This affects NGINX JavaScript versions 0.9.4 through 0.9.8, with fixes in njs 0.9.9.
doc_summary: NGINX has disclosed a high-severity vulnerability in its JavaScript module, tracked as CVE-2026-8711, which allows remote attackers to crash servers and potentially execute arbitrary code. The flaw is a heap-based buffer overflow in the NGINX JavaScript (njs) module, specifically when the js_fetch_proxy directive is used with client-controlled variables and ngx.fetch() calls. This vulnerability affects NGINX JavaScript versions 0.9.4 through 0.9.8, with fixes introduced in njs 0.9.9. F5 has published a security advisory (K000161307) detailing the issue, which can lead to denial-of-service (DoS) conditions and, in environments without ASLR, remote code execution (RCE). The vulnerability is rated as High (CVSS v3.1 8.1) and Critical (CVSS v4.0 9.2). Administrators are advised to upgrade to njs 0.9.9 or later to mitigate the risk.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain involves exploitation of a vulnerability in the NGINX JavaScript module, allowing attackers to send crafted HTTP requests that manipulate client-controlled variables, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. This can cause denial-of-service conditions and, in environments without ASLR, remote code execution. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-8711.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes a vulnerability (CVE-2026-8711) that can be exploited by sending crafted HTTP requests to NGINX servers. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The primary focus is on the vulnerability and its exploitation through client-controlled variables in the NGINX JavaScript module.

Title: DirtyDecrypt (DirtyCBC) Linux Kernel Vulnerability Exploitation

Victim.Description: Linux systems with CONFIG_RXGK enabled, including Fedora, Arch Linux, and Kubernetes worker nodes.

diamond_model_summary: The DirtyDecrypt vulnerability in the Linux kernel's RxGK security layer allows adversaries to escalate privileges to root on affected systems. The Zellic and V12 security team released a PoC exploit, targeting systems with CONFIG_RXGK enabled, primarily affecting Fedora and Arch Linux. The vulnerability involves decrypting RxGK RESPONSE tokens before verifying the MAC, allowing writes to page-cache pages of other processes or privileged files. The exploit poses risks in Kubernetes environments, granting attackers control over worker nodes. Fixes were introduced in April and May 2026, with recommendations to update kernels and monitor for suspicious activity.
doc_summary: The DirtyDecrypt (DirtyCBC) vulnerability in the Linux kernel's RxGK security layer for RxRPC transport, associated with CVE-2026-31635, allows local privilege escalation. The Zellic and V12 security team released a PoC exploit, turning a theoretical vulnerability into a practical exploit path to root on specific Linux distributions like Fedora and Arch Linux. The vulnerability involves decrypting RxGK RESPONSE tokens before verifying the MAC, allowing writes to page-cache pages of other processes or privileged files. The exploit affects kernels with CONFIG_RXGK enabled, posing risks in Kubernetes environments. Fixes were introduced in April and May 2026, with recommendations to update kernels and monitor for suspicious activity.
kill_chain_summary: The DirtyDecrypt vulnerability exploitation follows a structured kill chain. Initially, the adversary develops a PoC exploit for the vulnerability (Weaponization). The exploit is then used to gain root access on affected systems (Exploitation), primarily targeting Linux distributions with CONFIG_RXGK enabled. Once root access is achieved, the adversary gains control over system resources (Actions on Objectives). The exploitation poses significant risks in Kubernetes environments, allowing attackers to control worker nodes and access Kubernetes secrets. Detection and remediation involve updating kernels and monitoring for suspicious activity.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the DirtyDecrypt incident includes various indicators. The PoC exploit code represents a tool used by adversaries. The vulnerability CVE-2026-31635 is a key TTP employed in the attack. Monitoring for vulnerable kernel versions and CONFIG_RXGK settings is crucial for detection. Updating kernels with the latest patches and monitoring for suspicious activity related to RxGK module loading are recommended remediation steps. The Pyramid of Pain scoring reflects the significance of these indicators in detecting and mitigating the threat.

Their infrastructure includes Microsoft services, and they target organizations with high-value assets. doc_summary: Storm-2949, a threat actor, targets Microsoft 365 and Azure environments, exploiting legitimate applications and administration features to exfiltrate sensitive data. The actor uses social engineering to obtain Microsoft Entra ID credentials, abusing the Self-Service Password Reset flow and bypassing MFA. They leverage Microsoft Graph API and custom Python scripts for enumeration and persistence, accessing OneDrive and SharePoint for VPN configurations and IT files. Storm-2949 expands attacks to Azure infrastructure, exploiting RBAC roles to extract sensitive assets, deploy FTP, Web Deploy, and Kudu console, and modify Azure Key Vault access settings. They target Azure SQL servers and storage accounts, changing firewall rules and exfiltrating data. The actor deploys ScreenConnect, attempts to disable Microsoft Defender, and wipes forensic evidence. Microsoft recommends security hardening, least privilege, conditional access policies, and phishing-resistant MFA to defend against such attacks.
kill_chain_summary: Storm-2949's attack begins with reconnaissance through social engineering, targeting privileged users. They exploit the Self-Service Password Reset flow to gain access, bypass MFA, and install Microsoft Authenticator. Command and control are maintained via Microsoft Graph API and custom scripts. The actor's objectives include exfiltrating data from Microsoft 365 and Azure, modifying access settings, and deploying remote access tools.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for Storm-2949 includes tools like Microsoft Graph API and ScreenConnect, and TTPs such as social engineering and MFA bypass. doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed a new ad fraud and malvertising operation named Trapdoor targeting Android device users. The operation involved 455 malicious Android apps and 183 threat actor-owned command-and-control domains. Users unknowingly downloaded apps that triggered malvertising campaigns, coercing them into downloading additional threat actor-owned apps. These apps launched hidden WebViews, loaded threat actor-owned HTML5 domains, and requested ads. The campaign was self-sustaining, turning organic app installs into an illicit revenue generation cycle. At its peak, Trapdoor accounted for 659 million bid requests a day, with apps downloaded over 24 million times. Traffic primarily originated from the United States. The threat actors abused install attribution tools to enable malicious behavior only in users acquired through ad campaigns. Google has removed all identified malicious apps from the Play Store.

Delivery occurs via the Play Store, leading to exploitation as users download additional apps. Installation of secondary apps enables persistence and command and control through communication with domains. The final stage involves actions on objectives, where ad fraud is conducted to generate revenue. The operation's sophistication is evident in its use of obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques, as well as its selective activation of malicious behavior.

Victim.Description: Linux distributions with CONFIG_RXGK enabled, such as Fedora, Arch Linux, and openSUSE Tumbleweed.

diamond_model_summary: The DirtyDecrypt vulnerability in the Linux kernel represents a significant threat due to its potential for local privilege escalation. The incident highlights the need for rapid patching and potential use of emergency mitigations like the proposed killswitch.
doc_summary: Proof-of-concept exploit code released for DirtyDecrypt, a Linux kernel vulnerability allowing local privilege escalation. Discovered by Zellic and V12 security team, it affects distributions with CONFIG_RXGK enabled. The flaw, CVE-2026-31635, involves missing copy-on-write guard in rxgk_decrypt_skb function. Related to Copy Fail and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities, it impacts Fedora, Arch Linux, and openSUSE Tumbleweed. Security researcher Hyunwoo Kim disclosed details after embargo ended. Linux developers propose emergency killswitch for runtime mitigation. Rocky Linux offers optional security repository for urgent fixes.

Immediate patching and secure configuration are essential to defend against evolving threats targeting database infrastructure.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified a compromised version of the Nx Console extension in the Microsoft Visual Studio Code Marketplace. The attack avoided machines in Russian/CIS time zones and targeted secrets from 1Password, npm, GitHub, and AWS. The payload included Sigstore integration, allowing the attacker to publish npm packages with valid cryptographic signatures. Users were advised to update to version 18.100.0 or later and rotate all credentials.

The malware exfiltrates data to a command-and-control server at 87e0bbc636999b.lhr.life. The package supports HTTP, TCP, and UDP floods, and TCP reset attacks. doc_summary: Grafana Labs disclosed a breach where hackers, identified as the CoinbaseCartel extortion gang, accessed and downloaded its source code using a stolen access token. The gang, consisting of ShinyHunters and Lapsus$ affiliates, claimed responsibility by listing Grafana on their data leak site. Despite the breach, Grafana Labs reported no customer data exposure and followed FBI guidance by refusing to pay the ransom. The gang uses social engineering, phishing, and compromised credentials to infiltrate networks, deploying tools like shinysp1d3r for VMware ESXi encryption. Grafana Labs serves over 7,000 organizations, including large enterprises, cloud providers, and governments. The breach highlights the ongoing threat of cyber extortion and the importance of robust security measures.

Title: Phishing Campaign Targeting U.S. Organizations with Fake Invitations

Victim.Description: U.S. organizations in high-exposure industries were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The phishing campaign targeted U.S. organizations in high-exposure industries using fake invitations. The adversary's motivation was financial gain through credential theft and unauthorized access. The campaign used phishing emails with fake invitations and event-themed pages, potentially leading to credential theft, OTP capture, or delivery of legitimate RMM tools. doc_summary: A phishing campaign targeted U.S. organizations, particularly in sectors like Education, Banking, Government, Technology, and Healthcare. The attack involved fake invitations, CAPTCHA checks, and event-themed pages, potentially leading to credential theft, OTP capture, or delivery of legitimate RMM tools. ANY.RUN's interactive sandbox exposed the full attack chain, including redirects, fake pages, credential prompts, and signs of possible remote access. The campaign revealed repeatable patterns across phishing pages, such as requests to /favicon.ico, /blocked.html, and resources stored under /Image/*.png. This intelligence helps connect related domains, pages, and infrastructure. The campaign highlights the importance of early phishing detection and the use of interactive sandboxes to analyze suspicious emails and links. ANY.RUN offers threat intelligence solutions to expand phishing analysis capacity and improve SOC response workflows.
kill_chain_summary: The phishing campaign followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to gather information on target organizations. The adversary then weaponized phishing emails with fake invitations and event-themed pages. Delivery involved sending these emails to target organizations. Exploitation occurred when victims clicked on links, leading to credential theft. Installation potentially involved RMM tools for remote access. Command and control may have been established using web protocols. Finally, actions on objectives included using stolen credentials to access sensitive data.

The campaign highlights the importance of early phishing detection and the use of interactive sandboxes to analyze suspicious emails and links.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves attackers exploiting a vulnerability in NGINX, tracked as CVE-2026-42945. The adversary uses specially crafted HTTP requests to trigger a heap buffer overflow, potentially leading to remote code execution. The infrastructure at risk includes approximately 5.7 million internet-facing NGINX servers. Victims are organizations using vulnerable NGINX configurations, with a high exposure potential due to the widespread use of NGINX.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in NGINX, tracked as CVE-2026-42945, is being actively exploited. The flaw affects both NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus, allowing potential remote code execution and server crashes. Security researcher Patrick Garrity from VulnCheck reported that attackers are using specially crafted HTTP requests to trigger a heap buffer overflow in the NGINX worker process. This vulnerability does not require authentication, making it particularly dangerous. Exploitation depends on specific rewrite configurations, and systems with ASLR disabled are at higher risk. VulnCheck and Censys data indicate approximately 5.7 million internet-facing NGINX servers could be affected. Organizations are urged to review configurations, apply patches, and enable security protections like ASLR. The incident underscores the rapid weaponization of vulnerabilities in widely used infrastructure.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance where attackers scan for vulnerable NGINX servers. Weaponization involves crafting HTTP requests to exploit the vulnerability. Delivery occurs via these requests, leading to exploitation through a heap buffer overflow. The attack highlights the need for rapid patching and configuration reviews to mitigate risks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes HTTP request patterns as network host artifacts and the use of specific TTPs like heap buffer overflow. The scoring reflects the emphasis on network-level indicators.

The attackers' strategic objective is to gain unauthorized access to credentials and alter trusted software systems.
doc_summary: Supply chain attackers are targeting npm, PyPI, and Docker Hub to steal credentials from developer environments and CI/CD pipelines. Recent campaigns, including TeamPCP and Shai-Hulud, focus on credential theft, exposing secrets like API keys, cloud credentials, and SSH keys. Developer workstations are critical in the software supply chain, often containing sensitive data and credentials. Attackers use poisoned packages, compromised images, and malicious workflows to gain access. Automation and AI-assisted development increase the risk of rapid exploitation. Security teams must evaluate AI coding risks and implement guardrails to minimize exposure. The modern software supply chain starts at the developer workstation, where code, credentials, and automation intersect.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify developer environments and CI/CD pipelines. Weaponization involves creating malicious packages and workflows, followed by delivery through distribution to targets. Exploitation occurs as attackers steal credentials from developer environments. Installation of persistence mechanisms ensures continued access, while command and control is established through compromised systems. Finally, actions on objectives involve using stolen credentials to access and modify systems, highlighting the critical need for robust security measures at each stage.

Title: Supply Chain Attack via Malicious npm Packages

Victim.Description: Users and organizations that downloaded the malicious npm packages.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a single adversary, 'deadcode09284814', who used open-source malware to conduct a supply chain attack via npm packages. The adversary's capability includes deploying the Shai-Hulud worm and Phantom Bot for information stealing and DDoS attacks. The infrastructure involves multiple C2 servers for data exfiltration. Victims are users and organizations that downloaded the malicious packages, with high impact severity due to the theft of sensitive information.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered four malicious npm packages containing information-stealing malware. One package, 'chalk-tempalte', is a clone of the Shai-Hulud worm leaked by TeamPCP. The packages were published by 'deadcode09284814' and include 'axois-utils', which delivers a Golang-based DDoS botnet called Phantom Bot. The packages siphon SSH keys, environment variables, cloud credentials, system information, IP addresses, and cryptocurrency wallet data to remote servers. The attack highlights the growing threat of supply chain attacks and typo-squatting in the npm ecosystem. Users are advised to uninstall the packages, delete malicious configurations, rotate secrets, and block suspicious domains.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain starting with reconnaissance to identify npm packages for cloning. Weaponization involved using the Shai-Hulud worm and Phantom Bot. Delivery was executed through npm package downloads. Exploitation targeted the npm ecosystem. Installation involved persistence mechanisms on compromised systems. Command and control were established via C2 servers. Actions on objectives included data exfiltration and DDoS attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and domain names used for C2 communication, as well as the tools Phantom Bot and Shai-Hulud worm. These indicators are crucial for detection and response efforts. The adversary's use of open-source malware and typo-squatting techniques highlights the need for vigilance in monitoring npm package downloads and network traffic.

doc_summary: The Avada Builder plugin, used by over one million WordPress sites, was found to have two critical vulnerabilities: an arbitrary file read flaw (CVE-2026-4782) and a SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-4798). Discovered by Rafie Muhammad through the Wordfence Bug Bounty Program, these vulnerabilities allow both authenticated and unauthenticated attackers to compromise affected sites. The file read flaw affects versions up to 3.15.2, allowing attackers to read sensitive files like wp-config.php. The SQL injection flaw impacts versions up to 3.15.1, enabling time-based SQL injection attacks. Wordfence released firewall protections, and Avada issued patches in versions 3.15.2 and 3.15.3. Administrators are urged to update to version 3.15.3 to prevent data theft and site compromise.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-39987, in the Marimo Python notebook framework allows unauthenticated remote code execution via the /terminal/ws WebSocket endpoint. Title: Analysis of Fast16 Malware Targeting Nuclear Weapon Simulations

diamond_model_summary: The Fast16 incident involves a nation-state actor, likely the Equation Group, targeting nuclear weapons research through sophisticated malware. The malware, Fast16, is designed to tamper with specific simulation software, indicating a high level of domain knowledge and strategic intent to disrupt nuclear weapon development processes.
doc_summary: Fast16 is a Lua-based malware identified as a cyber sabotage tool targeting nuclear weapons testing simulations. Developed before Stuxnet, it was designed to corrupt uranium-compression simulations crucial for nuclear weapon design. Symantec and Carbon Black confirmed its targeting of LS-DYNA and AUTODYN applications, used for high-explosive simulations. The malware activates when material density exceeds 30 g/cm³, indicating uranium under implosion. Fast16's development dates back to 2005, predating Stuxnet by two years. Evidence links it to the Equation Group, with ties to the United States NSA. The malware features 101 hook rules, categorized into 9-10 groups, targeting different software versions. It avoids infection on systems with specific security products and spreads across networks. The incident highlights early nation-state industrial sabotage efforts.
kill_chain_summary: The Fast16 malware follows a structured kill chain, with weaponization involving the development of targeted malware to disrupt nuclear simulations. The actions on objectives stage is critical, where the malware activates under specific conditions to tamper with simulation outputs, highlighting a strategic sabotage effort by nation-state actors.

Title: MiniPlasma Zero-Day Vulnerability in Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver

Victim.Description: All Windows systems potentially affected by the MiniPlasma vulnerability.

diamond_model_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability represents a significant threat due to its ability to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on Windows systems. The adversary, Chaotic Eclipse, demonstrated high sophistication by identifying and weaponizing this zero-day flaw. The capability involves exploiting a race condition in the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver. The infrastructure details remain unspecified, but the victim scope is broad, affecting all Windows systems globally. The incident highlights the need for vigilance and timely patching to mitigate such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: Chaotic Eclipse, a security researcher, disclosed a Windows zero-day vulnerability named MiniPlasma affecting the Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver (cldflt.sys). This flaw allows privilege escalation to SYSTEM level on fully patched Windows systems. Originally reported by Google Project Zero's James Forshaw in September 2020, it was believed to be patched in December 2020 under CVE-2020-17103. However, Chaotic Eclipse found it remains unpatched. The vulnerability is a race condition in the HsmOsBlockPlaceholderAccess routine. Will Dormann confirmed MiniPlasma's effectiveness on Windows 11 with May 2026 updates, but not on Insider Preview Canary builds. Microsoft addressed a related flaw, CVE-2025-62221, in December 2025.
kill_chain_summary: The MiniPlasma incident follows a clear kill chain progression. Initially, the vulnerability was identified and weaponized by Chaotic Eclipse, who developed a PoC exploit. The exploitation stage involves leveraging the vulnerability to gain SYSTEM privileges on Windows systems. Actions on objectives include executing commands with elevated privileges. The incident underscores the importance of addressing vulnerabilities promptly to prevent exploitation. The lack of specific delivery and command and control stages suggests a focus on local exploitation rather than remote attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The MiniPlasma vulnerability presents a challenge at the higher levels of the Pyramid of Pain. The exploit itself is a zero-day, making it difficult to detect and mitigate without specific patches. The lack of specific indicators such as hashes, IP addresses, or domains further complicates detection efforts. The primary focus for defenders should be on understanding the TTPs associated with this vulnerability and implementing robust patch management practices. The incident highlights the critical need for proactive threat intelligence and vulnerability management to address such high-impact threats.

Title: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Claude Code via Crafted Deeplink

Victim.Description: Users of Claude Code, particularly those on macOS, were targeted.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary exploiting a vulnerability in Claude Code's CLI parsing logic to execute arbitrary commands. The capability was demonstrated through crafted deeplink URLs, targeting users of Claude Code, particularly on macOS. The infrastructure used involved malicious deeplink URLs, and the victims were users of Claude Code, primarily in the technology sector. The attack highlights the importance of secure parsing practices to prevent such vulnerabilities.
doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in Claude Code allowed attackers to execute arbitrary system commands through a crafted deeplink URL, exploiting a flaw in the CLI parsing logic. The issue was discovered by security researcher Joernchen and has been patched in version 2.1.118. The vulnerability originated from the eagerParseCliFlag function, which improperly parsed configuration flags, allowing attackers to inject malicious JSON settings objects. This led to remote code execution on macOS systems when users clicked on malicious claude-cli:// links. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, posing a significant threat to users who had cloned trusted repositories like anthropics/claude-code. The incident highlights the dangers of naive string parsing and underscores the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.
kill_chain_summary: The attack began with the weaponization of a crafted deeplink URL exploiting a CLI parsing flaw in Claude Code. The delivery stage involved sending the malicious URL to potential victims. Exploitation occurred when the victim clicked the link, triggering arbitrary command execution. The attack bypassed workspace trust dialogs, leading to actions on objectives, such as executing commands on the victim's system. The incident underscores the need for secure parsing and prompt patching of vulnerabilities.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of crafted deeplink URLs as a tool for exploitation. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains were identified. The primary TTP involved is the exploitation of a CLI parsing flaw, highlighting the need for secure parsing practices. The incident emphasizes the importance of context-aware argument parsing to prevent injection vulnerabilities.

Title: Tycoon2FA Phishing Kit Exploits Device-Code Phishing to Hijack Microsoft 365 Accounts

Victim.Description: Targets are users of Microsoft 365 services, potentially across various industries.

diamond_model_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit represents a sophisticated adversary employing advanced phishing techniques to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The adversary uses Trustifi click-tracking URLs and Cloudflare Workers to deliver phishing emails, tricking victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. The infrastructure includes obfuscated JavaScript layers and legitimate-looking phishing pages. Victims are primarily users of Microsoft 365 services, with a high impact severity due to unauthorized access to sensitive data.
doc_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit has been observed exploiting device-code phishing attacks to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. It abuses Trustifi click-tracking URLs to trick victims into granting OAuth tokens to attacker-controlled devices. Despite a law enforcement operation in March, the operation quickly resumed, adding new obfuscation layers. The attack involves an invoice-themed phishing email with a Trustifi tracking URL, redirecting through Cloudflare Workers and obfuscated JavaScript layers to a fake Microsoft CAPTCHA page. The phishing page retrieves a Microsoft OAuth device code, instructing victims to enter it at microsoft.com/devicelogin, leading to unauthorized access to the victim's data. eSentire's research highlights the kit's extensive protection against security tools and recommends disabling OAuth device code flow, restricting OAuth consent permissions, and monitoring Entra logs for suspicious activity.
kill_chain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance through phishing emails, weaponization with obfuscated JavaScript and Trustifi URLs, and delivery via phishing emails. Exploitation occurs when victims enter device codes on legitimate Microsoft pages, leading to installation of OAuth tokens on attacker-controlled devices. Command and control is achieved through unauthorized access to compromised accounts, and actions on objectives involve data access and exfiltration. The attack demonstrates a high level of sophistication and evasion tactics.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Tycoon2FA phishing kit presents significant challenges for defenders, with a focus on evasion and obfuscation. The pyramid of pain includes domain names like microsoft.com/devicelogin, tools such as Trustifi and Cloudflare Workers, and TTPs involving device-code phishing and OAuth token hijacking. The attack's sophistication and use of legitimate services make detection and mitigation difficult, emphasizing the need for advanced security measures and continuous monitoring.

doc_summary: A critical security flaw, CVE-2026-42945, affecting NGINX Plus and NGINX Open, has been actively exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, a heap buffer overflow in ngx_http_rewrite_module, impacts versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0 and was introduced in 2008. Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to crash worker processes or execute remote code, particularly when ASLR is disabled. VulnCheck detected exploitation attempts against its honeypot networks. Users are advised to apply the latest fixes from F5. The flaw requires specific NGINX configurations to be vulnerable, and exploitation is not trivial on systems with ASLR enabled. The attack activity's nature and goals remain unknown.

Detection involves monitoring network traffic and server logs, while remediation includes applying patches and enabling ASLR.

doc_summary: A security researcher identified a critical privilege escalation vulnerability in Azure Backup for AKS, allowing cluster-admin access from the low-privileged Backup Contributor role. Microsoft initially rejected the report, claiming the issue required pre-existing admin access. The researcher, Justin O'Leary, escalated the issue to CERT Coordination Center, which validated the vulnerability and assigned it VU#284781. Despite Microsoft's claim of no product changes, O'Leary observed new permission checks and failed exploit attempts, suggesting a silent patch. The vulnerability involved Azure RBAC and Kubernetes RBAC trust boundaries, allowing unauthorized cluster-admin access. Microsoft disputed the CVE issuance, leaving the vulnerability untracked. The case highlights challenges in vulnerability disclosure and the need for improved frameworks.

doc_summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel, identified as CVE-2026-46333 and dubbed ssh-keysign-pwn, exposes millions of systems to unauthorized access. The flaw, a race condition in the __ptrace_may_access() function, allows unprivileged local attackers to access sensitive SSH private keys and hashed passwords in /etc/shadow. This vulnerability, existing undetected for six years, affects major Linux distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS. Exploitation does not require elevated privileges, and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available. The vulnerability's impact includes impersonation attacks and offline password cracking. Linux kernel maintainers have released patches, and immediate updates are recommended.
kill_chain_summary: The ssh-keysign-pwn vulnerability follows a clear kill chain path. Exploitation occurs through a race condition in the Linux kernel, allowing local attackers to gain initial access to sensitive data. The lack of required elevated privileges simplifies the attack, enabling actions on objectives such as credential dumping and potential impersonation. Detection involves monitoring access to sensitive files and auditing ptrace permissions. Remediation requires immediate patching of affected systems and implementing strong access controls. The vulnerability's public disclosure and available proof-of-concept exploit increase the urgency for mitigation.

Remediation focuses on patching and access control, addressing the root cause of the vulnerability. A security advisory from the vendor confirms the malicious activity and recommends updating to the latest version and reviewing settings for rogue scripts.

This flaw allows attackers to execute AI workflows without credentials, affecting versions 2.5.6 through 4.6.33. The root cause is a legacy Flask-based API server with authentication disabled by default, hard-coding AUTH_ENABLED = False and AUTH_TOKEN = None. The vulnerability has been fixed in version 4.6.34. Users are advised to upgrade immediately or apply mitigation steps such as restricting network access and enabling authentication mechanisms. This incident highlights the risk of AI platforms shipping with insecure defaults, making them targets for attackers.

The flaw affects Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (vSmart) and SD-WAN Manager (vManage), allowing remote unauthenticated attackers to gain administrative control over enterprise networks. The attack surface includes cloud, on-premises, and government environments. Detection involves monitoring SSH log entries and control connections for anomalies. Rapid7 researchers Stephen Fewer and Jonah Burgess discovered the flaw, distinct from a previous Cisco SD-WAN issue. Organizations must upgrade to fixed software versions and conduct thorough compromise assessments.

doc_summary: The Belarus-aligned threat group Ghostwriter, also known as FrostyNeighbor, has been targeting Ukrainian governmental organizations since March 2026. doc_summary: Threat actors have been observed attempting to exploit a recently disclosed security vulnerability in PraisonAI, an open-source multi-agent orchestration framework, within four hours of public disclosure. The vulnerability, CVE-2026-44338, involves missing authentication that exposes sensitive endpoints, allowing attackers to invoke the API server's protected functionality without a token. The flaw affects all versions of the Python package from 2.5.6 through 4.6.33 and has been patched in version 4.6.34. Security researcher Shmulik Cohen discovered the bug. Sysdig reported that within three hours and 44 minutes of the advisory becoming public, a scanner identifying as CVE-Detector/1.0 probed the vulnerable endpoint on internet-exposed instances. The activity originated from IP address 146.190.133.49, with two passes spaced eight minutes apart. The first pass scanned generic disclosure paths, while the second targeted AI-agent surfaces, including PraisonAI. The rapid exploitation highlights a trend where threat actors quickly adopt newly disclosed flaws. Users are advised to apply the latest fixes, audit deployments, review billing for suspicious activity, and rotate credentials in agents.yaml.

doc_summary: CVE-2026-45185, also known as 'Dead.Letter', is a critical vulnerability in the Exim mail transfer agent affecting versions 4.97 through 4.99.2 when built with GnuTLS. This use-after-free vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution by exploiting Exim's handling of TLS-encrypted SMTP traffic and BDAT chunked message bodies. Successful exploitation can lead to complete mail server compromise, including reading or tampering with emails and deploying malware. doc_summary: An anonymous cybersecurity researcher, known as Chaotic Eclipse, disclosed two zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft products. The first, YellowKey, is a BitLocker bypass vulnerability in the Windows Recovery Environment, impacting Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025. It involves using specially crafted FsTx files on a USB drive to trigger a shell with BitLocker protections turned on. The second, GreenPlasma, is a privilege escalation vulnerability in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), allowing an unprivileged user to create arbitrary memory section objects. The vulnerabilities have been actively exploited, and Microsoft has been urged to address them promptly. Security researcher Will Dormann confirmed the YellowKey vulnerability, highlighting the ability of a System Volume Information\FsTx directory to modify another volume's contents. Intrinsec detailed an attack chain against BitLocker, leveraging a boot manager downgrade to bypass encryption protection. Microsoft plans to retire old PCA 2011 certificates to mitigate risks.
